# AGENTS.md

Regras para agentes que editam o repositório **RoosterEdit**. Leia este arquivo antes de qualquer mudança.

Ordem de precedência em caso de conflito:

1. `AGENTS.md` — processo e limites do repositório.
2. `SKILL.md` + `references/` — contrato da skill (em inglês).
3. Código em `scripts/` — comportamento real.
4. `docs/` — documentação humana (em pt-BR).

Se o código contradiz a documentação, o código vence para descrever o comportamento; corrija a documentação ou registre a divergência.

---

## 1. O que é este repositório

- A raiz do repositório **é o pacote da skill**. Não é um workspace de vídeo.
- `scripts/rooster.mjs` é o CLI (Node.js, ESM, zero dependências de runtime).
- `scripts/lib/` guarda infraestrutura: cache, exec async, capabilities, engines, media, ASR, build, render.
- `scripts/features/` guarda helpers puros (args de FFmpeg, legendas, gráficos, áudio, motion).
- `scripts/test/` guarda testes com `node:test` (zero dependências).
- `references/` e `agents/` fazem parte da skill instalável e são escritos em inglês.
- `docs/` é documentação humana durável, em pt-BR.
- `.opencode/skills/rooster-edit/` é uma **cópia gerada** por `scripts/sync-skill.mjs`. Nunca edite essa cópia; edite a raiz e rode o sync.
- `rooster/` é o workspace padrão de vídeo do usuário. É ignorado pelo git e não deve ser criado na raiz para testes.

## 2. O que ler antes de trabalhar

| Tarefa | Leia primeiro |
|---|---|
| Qualquer mudança | `AGENTS.md` (este arquivo) |
| Skill, fluxo, comandos | `SKILL.md` |
| Edição, plano, timeline, QA | o reference específico em `references/` |
| Arquitetura e decisões | `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` |
| Workspace, canais, perfis | `docs/WORKSPACE.md` |
| Testes já feitos | `docs/TESTING.md` |
| Custo e licenças | `docs/COSTS.md`, `references/assets.md` |

Não leia o repositório inteiro por padrão. Leia só o reference da fase atual.

## 3. Idioma

- `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `agents/` e comentários de código: **inglês**.
- `README.md`, `docs/` e este `AGENTS.md`: **pt-BR**.
- Respostas ao usuário: no idioma da conversa.
- Não traduza nomes de comandos, campos de JSON, schemas ou paths.

## 4. Durable vs temporal (regra dura)

`docs/` é somente para documentação **durável**, que deve sobreviver a releases e ser mantida.

**Não coloque em `docs/`:**

- auditorias;
- benchmarks e medições de uma tarefa;
- relatórios de uma sessão;
- rascunhos, análises exploratórias, listas de ideias;
- resultados gerados, logs, frames, contact sheets;
- qualquer arquivo que comece com data ou nome de projeto.

**Coloque em `.scratch/`** (ignorado pelo git), com prefixo de data:

```text
.scratch/2026-11-03-performance-audit.md
.scratch/2026-11-05-render-bench.json
.scratch/2026-11-07-ideias-de-ux.md
```

Regras:

- `.scratch/` é descartável. Pode apagar sem aviso quando o assunto morrer.
- Não linke `.scratch/` no README nem em `docs/`.
- Se um achado virar regra permanente, destile-o no lugar certo (`docs/`, `references/` ou `ROADMAP.md`) e apague o scratch.
- Logs de execução de um projeto de vídeo ficam em `work/logs/` dentro do workspace do projeto, não no repositório.
- Benchmarks de uma máquina não viram documentação oficial sem protocolo reproduzível e data.

## 5. Dados do usuário e segurança

- Nunca apague ou sobrescreva mídia original do usuário.
- Não rode comandos destrutivos (`rm -rf`, `Remove-Item -Recurse`, `--force`) fora de diretórios de teste.
- Para testes, use `ROOSTER_WORKSPACE` apontando para um diretório temporário e limpe depois.
- Não commite `.env`, chaves, cookies, tokens, mídia, renders, caches ou logs.
- Não chame API paga, TTS pago ou render em nuvem sem permissão explícita.
- Não faça upload de mídia do usuário.
- Respeite licenças e proveniência de assets; não invente licença.

## 6. Regras de código

- Node.js `>=20`, ESM (`import`/`export`), zero dependências de runtime.
- Não adicione pacote npm sem pedido explícito; prefira a biblioteca padrão.
- Mantenha o padrão de helpers existente: `run`, `readJson`, `writeJson`, `writeText`, `ensureDir`, `fail`, `probeMedia`, `linkOrCopy`.
- Lógica pura de features fica em `scripts/features/`; infraestrutura com I/O/processos fica em `scripts/lib/`; o CLI e o dispatcher ficam em `scripts/rooster.mjs`.
- Testes automatizados ficam em `scripts/test/` e usam `node:test`; não crie dependências de teste.
- Evite refatorações grandes não pedidas. O arquivo principal é grande de propósito; mexer nele exige cuidado.
- Compatibilidade com Windows: paths com `path.join`, spawn de `.cmd` via `cmd.exe`, sem comandos bash-only.
- `spawnSync` é o padrão atual. Se precisar de paralelismo, introduza um helper isolado e não mude o comportamento existente sem teste.
- Saída humana no stdout; `--json` estável e parseável para agentes.
- Erros devem dizer o que falhou e como corrigir; use `fail()` para encerrar com código 1.
- Não esconda falha atrás de fallback silencioso. Se degradar, avise.

## 7. Mudou o CLI? Checklist

Toda mudança de comportamento precisa atualizar os pontos abaixo, quando aplicável:

1. Implementação em `scripts/rooster.mjs` ou `scripts/features/`.
2. Texto de ajuda/usage no próprio CLI.
3. `SKILL.md` (comandos rápidos e contrato), se for comando ou comportamento de usuário.
4. Reference correspondente em `references/` (ex.: `edit-plan.md`, `engines.md`, `schemas.md`).
5. `templates/` se o schema de plano/perfil mudou.
6. `docs/` apenas se for conhecimento durável.
7. `npm run validate`.
8. Smoke test em workspace temporário.
9. `node scripts/sync-skill.mjs` se quiser testar a descoberta local no OpenCode (a cópia é gerada; não commite).

Não anuncie um comando como pronto sem rodá-lo. Se não deu para testar, diga o que falta.

## 8. Documentação

- `docs/` é durável: precisa de propósito claro e manutenção.
- Não duplique `SKILL.md`; linke.
- Mantenha o índice de documentação do `README.md` atualizado ao adicionar um doc durável.
- Comandos devem ser copiáveis, usando `<skill>` para o caminho da skill.
- Números de performance só entram em doc durável se tiverem protocolo reproduzível.
- Relatórios temporários vão para `.scratch/` (ver seção 4).

## 9. Testes e validação

- `npm run validate` é obrigatório antes de concluir.
- `npm test` roda os testes unitários (`node --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs`) e também é obrigatório quando a mudança toca `scripts/lib/`, `scripts/features/` ou schemas.
- Smoke test mínimo do CLI:

```bash
node scripts/rooster.mjs --help
node scripts/rooster.mjs doctor --json
```

- Para mudanças de fluxo, teste em workspace temporário:

```bash
$env:ROOSTER_WORKSPACE = "$env:TEMP\rooster-test"
node scripts/rooster.mjs init
node scripts/rooster.mjs channel new demo --language pt-BR --format 16:9 --profile minimal
node scripts/rooster.mjs channel design demo --from minimal --accent "#22d3ee"
node scripts/rooster.mjs new teste --channel demo
```

- Não existe suíte de testes formal. `docs/TESTING.md` é um registro de testes manuais, não uma suíte automatizada.
- Se adicionar testes automatizados, use `node:test` e mantenha zero dependências.
- Teste o caminho de erro também: arquivo ausente, plano inválido, ffmpeg indisponível.
- Em Windows, cuidado com handles de arquivo e hardlinks; valide o comportamento no SO alvo.

## 10. Sync da skill

- Fonte de verdade: a raiz do repositório.
- `.opencode/skills/rooster-edit/` é artefato de build local, ignorado pelo git.
- Rode `npm run sync` (ou `node scripts/sync-skill.mjs`) depois de mudar `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `scripts/`, `templates/` ou `agents/`, se precisar testar no OpenCode.
- Nunca edite arquivos em `.opencode/` diretamente.

## 11. Performance

- Meça antes de otimizar. Benchmarks e resultados vão para `.scratch/` ou `work/logs/`, não para `docs/`.
- Cache só entra com chave de invalidação (conteúdo + versão da ferramenta + opções) e opção de `--refresh`.
- Não troque qualidade por velocidade silenciosamente: draft e final são explícitos.
- Hardware encode só em draft/intermediário, salvo validação de qualidade para entrega.
- Não adicione paralelismo sem limite; Chrome/ffmpeg consomem RAM e CPU.
- Se um relatório de performance for pedido, o default é `.scratch/YYYY-MM-DD-performance-*.md`.

## 12. Git e commits

- Commits pequenos e focados.
- Estilo convencional: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `refactor:`.
- Não commite artefatos gerados: `.opencode/`, `rooster/`, `.rooster/`, `.scratch/`, renders, mídia, logs.
- Não reescreva histórico nem faça force-push sem permissão.
- Não misture mudança de código com relatório temporal no mesmo commit.
- Se o usuário pedir para manter um scratch, pergunte onde promovê-lo antes de mover para `docs/`.

## 13. Quando a tarefa é produzir vídeo

- Siga `SKILL.md` e o fluxo de 6/8 etapas.
- Não renderize antes do plano e do preview aprovados, salvo pedido explícito.
- Use o workspace do projeto; não crie projeto na raiz do repositório da skill.
- Delegue etapas pesadas a subagents quando o harness permitir; o principal lê handoff, não transcrição/log/código gerado.
- Feche a tarefa com resultado, caminhos, bloqueios e uma próxima pergunta.

## 14. Armadilhas comuns

- `.opencode/skills/rooster-edit/` é gerado; editar ali não muda a skill.
- `docs/` não é lugar de relatório temporário; use `.scratch/`.
- `references/` é contrato da skill em inglês; não traduza.
- `rooster/` na raiz é workspace de vídeo, não pasta de teste do repositório.
- `doctor` pode chamar `npx` e demorar; não o coloque em loop de teste.
- `build --force` apaga o diretório do engine; nunca aponte para projeto do usuário sem intenção.
- `linkOrCopy` usa hardlink quando possível; em outro volume vira cópia.
- Windows pode segurar handles; espere antes de apagar diretórios grandes.
- Não presuma que uma lib está instalada; cheque versão e adapter real.

## 15. Comandos rápidos

```bash
npm run validate
npm test
npm run sync
node scripts/rooster.mjs --help
node scripts/rooster.mjs doctor --json
```

Se algo não estiver claro, pergunte antes de inventar uma convenção nova.

# RoosterEdit

RoosterEdit is a video studio for agents. It does not replace Remotion, HyperFrames, or FFmpeg; it decides what to make, organizes the assets, writes the plan, drives the chosen engine, reviews the result, and delivers the package.

The most important rule: **do not render before the plan and the preview are approved**, unless the user explicitly asks for no stops. Rendering is the cheapest part of the pipeline and the most expensive mistake to undo.

### Running the CLI

This skill ships its CLI at `scripts/rooster.mjs` relative to the skill's base directory. Run it from the user's project directory, resolving the script against the skill base. In the examples below, `<skill>` means that base directory:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" doctor --json
```

Do not create a `scripts/` directory in the user's project just to satisfy the command. The workspace (`rooster/`) belongs to the project; the CLI belongs to the skill. If the shell's working directory is the skill directory, the CLI will create the workspace in the wrong place.

## Where to install the skill

When the user asks you to install RoosterEdit, ask first whether the install should be **local to the project (recommended)** or **global**. Use the skill folder the current harness actually reads; do not assume OpenCode.

- **Local:** the harness's project-level skill folder plus `rooster-edit` (for example `.opencode/skills`, `.claude/skills`, or `.agents/skills`). Recommended because the version stays with the project and cannot surprise other work.
- **Global:** the harness's global skill folder plus `rooster-edit` (for example `~/.config/opencode/skills` or `~/.claude/skills`). Use it only when the user wants RoosterEdit in every project on the machine.

If you cannot determine the harness's folders, inspect its skill discovery paths or ask the user. Wait for the answer before cloning. This choice is about where the skill lives, not where the video workspace lives (`./rooster`).

### Reporting

End-of-task replies are short by default: 5-10 lines or one compact table. Include only what the user needs to act:

- what was done or found;
- the paths or links to the result;
- what is missing or blocked, if anything;
- one clear next question.

Do not repeat the brief, paste logs, list every command, or explain the whole skill unless the user asks. Put details in workspace files or link the reference docs. A plan, QA report, or delivery package can be longer only because the user must review its contents.

Installation and workspace setup are separate steps. After installing and running `doctor`, do not start onboarding or write a guide. Summarize the environment in a few lines and ask whether the user wants to configure the workspace now. Wait for a yes before creating `rooster/` or a channel.

### Progress updates

Use a compact step marker in status updates and at every approval gate. Keep one 8-step tracker for the project:

1. Environment and workspace
2. Brief and intake
3. Assets and transcript
4. Edit plan
5. Storyboard and timeline
6. Engine choice and build
7. Preview and QA
8. Render and delivery

Examples:

- `Etapa 3/8 — Transcrição concluída. 42 trechos, 10:12 de duração.`
- `Etapa 4/8 — Plano pronto em edit/plan.html. Posso seguir com a timeline?`
- `Etapa 6/8 — Plano aprovado. Quer HyperFrames, Remotion (instalar) ou FilmCraft (conectar o MCP)?`
- `Etapa 6/8 — Build concluído. Posso abrir o preview e rodar o QA?`
- `Etapa 8/8 — Preview aprovado. Posso renderizar o final?`

Skip steps that do not apply and say why. Do not print the full checklist on every message; show the current step, what changed, and the next gate. Do not combine timeline and final render in one approval: preview and QA sit between them. Step 6 starts with the engine/timeline question; do not build before the user answers or explicitly delegates the choice.

## Subagent-first execution

The main agent is the director, not the worker. It talks to the user, owns the brief and the decisions, runs the approval gates, and looks at the final frames. The noisy work goes to a stage subagent: transcript analysis, research, script drafts, plan drafts, style and storyboard, build and fixes, QA sweeps, render and packaging. Each subagent has its own context, which is discarded when the stage ends, so raw material never accumulates in the main thread.

Delegate by default whenever the harness has a subagent tool. Keep the stage inline when it is one cheap command, when it is the conversation itself (intake, approvals), or when it is the final visual judgment.

| Stage | Subagent | Main agent receives |
|---|---|---|
| Brief | `producer` | one-paragraph brief + open questions |
| Research | `researcher` | 5 findings + sources + license flags |
| Transcript | `transcript-analyst` | duration, topics, 10–20 beats, flags |
| Script | `scriptwriter` | hook + beat summary |
| Plan | `editor` | plan summary + risks |
| Style/storyboard | `art-director` | tokens + scene count + asset needs |
| Timeline | `editor` | duration math + markers |
| Audio | `audio-director` | voice/music/mix decisions |
| Build | `engineer` | status + artifact paths + blocker |
| QA | `qa` | verdict + top issues + frame paths |
| Render | `engineer` | final path + probe stats |

Spawn with a short prompt: role file path, project path, one task sentence, input paths, constraints. Pass paths, never the brief, transcript, logs, or plan contents. If the input is the conversation itself, write the answers to `work/intake.md` first. Ask for the handoff described in `references/subagents.md` and nothing else. Use the harness's general-purpose or worker agent for stages that write files or run commands; a read-only or research type is fine for research. This is a capability, not a tool name: if the harness cannot start a fresh agent with file and command access, or a spawn fails twice, run the stage inline and keep the file boundaries.

The handoff is the only thing that enters the main context:

```text
status: ok | needs-decision | blocked
artifacts: paths that exist
summary: <= 5 lines
decisions: what the main agent must confirm
blockers: what stops the stage
next: next stage or exact question
```

The main agent may read the brief, script, style, `review.md`, and handoffs, and may view `plan.html` and 3–5 frames. It must not read the raw transcript, full plan JSON, generated code, build/render logs, or a contact sheet of dozens of frames. If a detail is missing, send a follow-up to the same subagent instead of opening the raw file.

Nothing here is a dependency. The artifacts and gates are the same when a stage runs inline; you lose the context isolation, not the workflow.

Approval gates never move to a subagent. The subagent proposes; the user and the main agent decide.

## First run after installation

If the workspace does not exist yet, do a short onboarding before creating any project. The workspace is created as part of the channel step; do not ask where it lives.

**First ask (one message):** "Quer criar o primeiro canal agora? Pensa nele como a pasta daquele projeto: dentro dela ficam os vídeos, o estilo e os arquivos da marca ou cliente. Se sim, me diga o nome do canal e o que ele vai produzir?"

If the answer is no, stop and create nothing. If they answer only one part, ask for the missing name or content.

If the answer is yes:

1. Use the name the user gave (slugified) as the channel id. If they described the content but gave no name, propose a short kebab-case name and confirm it.
2. Use the content sentence verbatim and infer language, format, source, assets, engine, autonomy, and voice. Keep the profile at `minimal` for now; the identity step defines it. Do not infer a visual style from the topic. Do not ask for a duration.
3. Show the inferred defaults in one compact line and ask "Está bom ou quer ajustar algo?" Ask a follow-up only when a field is genuinely ambiguous, such as the platform or whether the source is real footage.
4. On confirmation, run `init`, then `channel new <id> ...` with the answers.
5. Create the channel identity: ask three questions (palette, typography, motion/audio) and run `channel design <id> ...`. This writes `channels/<id>/profiles/<id>/profile.json` + `STYLE.md` and sets `channel.profile`. Show a short summary and stop.

During first-run, run `filmcraft status --json` once. If `prompt.kind` is `connect-mcp` or `install`, ask the question in `prompt` before creating the first project:

- CLI found, MCP not registered: "I found FilmCraft <version> on your PC. Do you want to connect its MCP now? After connecting, you must restart the program/agent so it can see the tools." (Connect MCP / Not now)
- FilmCraft not found: "I did not find FilmCraft on your PC. Do you want to continue with HyperFrames/Remotion, or install FilmCraft and connect its MCP?" (Continue with HyperFrames/Remotion / Install FilmCraft + connect MCP)

If the user declines, continue with HyperFrames/Remotion and do not ask again for that project. If the MCP is already registered, mention that a restart may still be needed if the tools are not visible. Never install FilmCraft or write MCP config without explicit permission. Read `references/onboarding.md` for the CLI-missing and already-registered cases.

Duration is an outcome of the edit, not a channel default and not a project default. Trimming silence and cuts change the length. `--duration` exists only for a target the user explicitly declares; otherwise the plan and the media define the final length. The full twelve-field setup is an opt-in advanced path. If the user asks to customize everything, ask in groups of at most three, never all at once.

A channel is the stable group for a brand, audience, or operation (for example "Studio A" or "Client B"). It owns the creative defaults: language, format, profile, assets policy, engine, autonomy, and voice. Every project belongs to a channel and can override any of those defaults. Duration comes from the edit; a channel or project only carries a target when the user declares one.

Do not start a video in the same turn unless the user explicitly asks. Read `references/onboarding.md` for the exact questions, defaults, and commands. Read `references/assets.md` before downloading or generating any asset.

## Fast path: the 6-step video workflow

When the user wants the simplest route from raw footage to a finished video, follow the same six steps as the reference workflow, adapted to the RoosterEdit workspace:

1. **Prepare the machine** — FFmpeg, Node.js LTS, Python 3, HyperFrames, and Whisper (or HyperFrames' Parakeet/whisper.cpp). Ask before installing anything.
2. **Create or resolve the project** — `rooster new ...`; raw media goes in `assets/source/`.
3. **Write the style guide** — `art-director` writes `style.md` and resolves the profile. Run `styleproof <slug>` and approve the three sample frames before planning.
4. **Transcribe and plan** — `transcript-analyst` writes `edit/transcript.json`, `edit/digest.md`, and `edit/analysis.json`; `editor` writes `edit/plan.json` from the analysis and `style.md`. Show `plan.html` with transcript context and wait for approval.
5. **Create the visual elements** — `engineer` builds letreiros, graphics, lists, zooms, b-roll, lower thirds, music, and SFX when the channel style calls for them. A cut-only draft is not a finished video unless the user explicitly asked for a clean cut.
6. **Assemble, review, export** — `engineer` runs `build` to generate the HyperFrames or Remotion project from the approved plan; use `--sample 3` before the full build. `qa` inspects `preview/index.html` and the frames, then `engineer` renders to `renders/`; `export` writes an EDL/FCPXML handoff when the user wants DaVinci or Premiere.

Read `references/video-pipeline.md` for the exact commands and the mapping from the reference video's folders to ours. The rest of this skill is the broader studio mode; the fast path is the default for single-video jobs.

## Operating principles

- **Direct before generating.** A clear brief, script, and shot list save more time than any prompt tweak. Spend the first part of the work understanding the video.
- **Inspect, don't assume.** Read the files, probe the media, look at frames, and check the tools. Never claim a render or an asset exists because the code looks right.
- **Keep the edit editable.** Prefer named scenes, variables, and readable components over one-off scripts. The user should be able to change a color, a line, or a clip without rewriting the project.
- **Review with eyes.** Use the browser preview, screenshots, or rendered stills to judge composition, pacing, and captions. Code review alone is not enough.
- **Respect provenance.** Record where every asset came from and its license. A beautiful video with an unlicensed track is a liability.
- **Degrade gracefully.** The harness may not have subagents, a browser, Node, FFmpeg, or TTS. Offer the best path available and say what is missing.
- **Delegate the heavy stages.** The main agent directs; stage subagents do the noisy work and return a short handoff. Transcripts, build logs, generated code, and QA sweeps should not pass through the main context. Read `references/subagents.md`.
- **Report short.** End every task with the result, the paths, and one next question. Do not narrate the whole process or dump commands unless the user asks.
- **Finish the creative layer.** Cuts alone are not a video. Plan overlays, b-roll, music, SFX, or captions unless the user explicitly asked for a clean cut.
- **Ask when uncertain.** If a choice changes the cut, the look, the audio, or the cost, ask at the current `Etapa X/8`. Do not guess silently.
- **Protect the context.** Video work is token-heavy. Redirect engine logs to files, read only the tail, use `digest` instead of the full transcript, and inspect a few key frames instead of every frame. Read `references/token-discipline.md`.

## Step 0 - Find the workspace

Look for a `rooster/` directory in the current project first, then use `ROOSTER_WORKSPACE` if it is set. The default is `./rooster`; only ask for a custom path when the user wants one.

If neither exists and the user has already asked to make a video, creating the workspace is implied; run:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" init
```

If the user just installed the skill or is only exploring, do not create it silently: follow "First run after installation" and ask first.

The workspace is where **channels**, projects, profiles, and the asset library live. Keep it out of the skill directory; the skill is reusable, the workspace belongs to the user's video project.

If the workspace exists but has no channel, create one before creating a project. Every project belongs to a channel; a `default` channel covers one-off videos.

If the user is only asking a question or exploring an idea, answer it without creating a workspace. A question is not a request to build.

## Modes

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `auto` | Make sensible decisions, log them, stop only for missing assets, license issues, or render failures |
| `guided` | Stop at brief, script, style/storyboard, rough cut, and final approval |
| `manual` | The user provides the script, EDL, or assets; execute precisely and ask before changing creative decisions |

Source, voice, and style are independent flags. A real-footage video can use TTS narration; a generated video can use the user's voice; a 3D video can have no voice at all.

## Workspace contract

The skill expects this shape:

```text
rooster/
├── workspace.json
├── config.json
├── channels/<channel>/
│   ├── channel.json
│   ├── projects/<slug>/
│   │   ├── project.json
│   │   ├── brief.md
│   │   ├── script.md
│   │   ├── style.md
│   │   ├── style/proof/
│   │   ├── storyboard/
│   │   ├── assets/{source,generated,licensed}/
│   │   ├── edit/{transcript.json,digest.md,analysis.json,plan.json,plan.md,plan.html,timeline.json,edl.json,captions/,audio/,export/}
│   │   ├── engine/{hyperframes|remotion|ffmpeg|filmcraft}/
│   │   ├── work/{handoffs,logs,scratch,notes}/
│   │   ├── preview/
│   │   ├── renders/
│   │   ├── qa/{report.md,text-review.md,frames/}
│   │   └── review.md
│   ├── profiles/<id>/
│   ├── assets/
│   └── library/
├── profiles/<id>/
├── library/{music,sfx,fonts,overlays,luts,broll,images}/
└── cache/
```

New projects belong inside `channels/<channel>/projects/`. The root `projects/` folder is legacy; only keep it for old workspaces.

If the user already has a different structure, adapt to it and record the mapping in `project.json` instead of forcing a migration.

## Guardrails

- Do not render with missing assets. A placeholder is a bug, not a style.
- Do not cover the footage with a full-screen panel or card unless the user explicitly asks for it. Prefer lower-thirds, captions, corner labels, and overlays that leave the video visible. A mismatched slide is not an invitation to cover the screen.
- Do not use unlicensed music, fonts, or footage. If the license is unknown, ask.
- Do not download third-party video from a link unless the user owns it or has permission; respect platform terms and copyright. Never bypass DRM, paywalls, or access controls.
- Do not upload, publish, or send files to external services without explicit consent.
- Do not run destructive shell commands on the user's source media.
- Do not hide a failure behind a lower-quality render. Report it.
- Do not claim a feature is supported because a library exists; check the installed version and the actual adapter.
- Do not create a full NLE, a video-generation model, or a cloud render service as part of the v1 scope. Keep the core focused and pluggable.

## What good looks like

A good RoosterEdit session feels like working with a director who also knows the tools:

- the user explains the idea in a few sentences;
- the agent asks two or three sharp questions, not twenty;
- the plan appears as a brief, a script, and a storyboard the user can react to;
- the style is consistent because it comes from a profile, not from vibes;
- three style-proof frames and three sample elements are approved before the full build;
- the preview is visible in the browser before the expensive render;
- every on-screen text is proofread and every cut boundary was checked by ear;
- the final package includes the video, captions, thumbnail, and metadata;
- the next video starts faster because the profile or component was saved and the channel already holds the defaults.

RoosterEdit

Um estúdio de vídeo para agentes de IA.
Você traz a ideia e o material. O agente cuida do plano, da edição e do render.

Instalação · Como funciona · Primeiro vídeo · Motores · Documentação

RoosterEdit é uma skill que ensina agentes de IA a trabalhar com vídeo. Ela junta transcrição, plano de edição, cortes e render em um fluxo só, do material bruto ao arquivo final. Com o RoosterEdit você edita gravações, cria vídeos narrados com imagens e gráficos, monta cenas em 3D e produz conteúdo para redes sociais. Você escolhe o formato, o estilo e a ferramenta de render, HyperFrames ou Remotion. O agente cuida do projeto do começo ao fim.

## O que já funciona - Organizar materiais por canais, com idioma, formato, estilo, voz e política de assets. - Transcrever com HyperFrames/Parakeet ou Whisper. - Montar um plano com cortes, capítulos, elementos visuais, b-roll e música. - Aprovar 3 frames de estilo e 3 elementos de amostra antes do build completo. - Gerar o projeto em HyperFrames ou Remotion já com os cortes e a música aplicados. - Revisar o plano e a timeline no browser com player, contexto da transcrição e QA. - Listar todos os textos em tela e avisar sobre cortes no meio de palavras. - Exportar EDL/FCPXML para finalizar no DaVinci Resolve ou Premiere. - Montar uma timeline editável no FilmCraft (opcional), com clipes de elemento separados. +- Gerar um rascunho de issue de feedback com dados sensíveis removidos quando algo falha no caminho. - Baixar links autorizados com `yt-dlp`. - Usar perfis prontos ou criar os seus. - Revisar no preview e renderizar o arquivo final. ## Como funciona 1. Você configura um canal. Ele guarda o que não muda de vídeo para vídeo: idioma, formato, estilo, voz e de onde vêm os assets. 2. Coloca o material bruto no projeto. 3. O agente transcreve, entende o conteúdo e escreve o plano de edição com cortes, elementos visuais, b-roll e música. 4. Você lê o plano, ajusta o que quiser e aprova. 5. Só então o projeto é gerado, pré-visualizado e renderizado. O plano é o ponto de controle. Ele vira um artefato revisável antes do preview e do render. Se ele estiver errado, o vídeo inteiro sai errado. ## As 8 etapas O agente acompanha o projeto com um marcador `Etapa X/8` e só avança nos gates de aprovação. Etapas que não se aplicam são puladas com uma explicação curta. | Etapa | O que acontece | Você aprova | |---|---|---| | 1. Ambiente e workspace | doctor, workspace e canal | — | | 2. Brief e intake | objetivo, público, formato, duração (só se você declarar) e restrições | brief | | 3. Assets e transcrição | material, probe, transcrição e mapa editorial | — | | 4. Plano de edição | cortes, elementos, música e capítulos | plano | | 5. Storyboard e timeline | cenas, tempos, legendas e áudio | storyboard/timeline | | 6. Escolha do engine e build | HyperFrames, Remotion ou FilmCraft; depois o projeto | engine/timeline e sample | | 7. Preview e QA | preview no browser, frames e checklist | preview | | 8. Render e entrega | draft, final, thumbnail e metadata | render final | Na etapa 6, o agente pergunta como montar: **HyperFrames** (padrão, já pronto), **Remotion** (React/3D; precisa de `npm install` com a sua permissão) ou **FilmCraft** (timeline editável; precisa conectar o MCP e reiniciar o agente). Nada é instalado nem configurado sem você autorizar. As etapas pesadas podem rodar em subagents para economizar contexto, mas o fluxo é o mesmo sem eles: os artefatos e os gates não mudam. Antes do plano, peça 3 frames de amostra do estilo (`styleproof`); antes do build completo, peça 3 elementos de amostra (`build --sample 3`). Isso evita refazer o vídeo inteiro por causa do look. ## Instalação A instalação é feita pelo seu agente. Ele pergunta se você quer instalar localmente no projeto (recomendado) ou globalmente, usando a pasta de skills que o seu harness lê, clona a skill, confere Node, FFmpeg e o browser, responde em poucas linhas e pergunta se você quer criar o primeiro canal. Você não precisa rodar comandos no terminal: o agente executa e mostra o resultado. Se quiser o prompt único de instalação + dependências + workspace, use [`templates/install-prompt.pt-BR.md`](templates/install-prompt.pt-BR.md). Custos esperados estão em [`docs/COSTS.md`](docs/COSTS.md). Copie o prompt abaixo e cole na conversa com o seu agente: ```text Instale a skill RoosterEdit neste projeto e valide o ambiente. 1. Antes de clonar, pergunte se quero instalação local no projeto (recomendado) ou global. Use a pasta de skills que este harness já lê; exemplos de local: `.opencode/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`; exemplos de global: `~/.config/opencode/skills`, `~/.claude/skills`. Não clone nada antes da minha resposta. 2. Clone https://github.com/WesleyQDev/RoosterEdit.git na pasta escolhida, com o nome rooster-edit. 3. Confirme que o arquivo SKILL.md está no lugar. 4. Rode o doctor da skill e me mostre só o essencial: o que está pronto e o que falta, em no máximo 6 linhas. 5. Se faltar Node.js, FFmpeg ou FFprobe, me peça permissão antes de instalar qualquer coisa e explique o comando. 6. Não crie workspace, projeto ou vídeo ainda. Só instale a skill e valide o ambiente. 7. No fim, responda em no máximo 8 linhas: status da instalação, o que já está pronto, o que falta (se algo) e onde ler os detalhes. Não escreva um guia longo nem liste todos os comandos. 8. Termine com uma pergunta simples: "Quer criar o primeiro canal agora? Pensa nele como a pasta daquele projeto: dentro dela ficam os vídeos, o estilo e os arquivos da marca ou cliente. Se sim, me diga o nome do canal e o que ele vai produzir?" Se eu disser não, pare sem criar nada. 9. Se eu disser sim, use o nome que eu der (ou proponha um), infira os padrões e me mostre um resumo para ajustar. Não faça as 12 perguntas de uma vez e não defina duração. 10. Depois do canal, pergunte paleta, tipografia e motion/áudio e crie a identidade com `channel design `. Se eu não tiver preferência, mantenha o perfil base. ``` Se preferir o caminho manual, o passo a passo completo está em [`docs/INSTALL.md`](docs/INSTALL.md). ## Primeiro vídeo Peça ao agente algo como "quero fazer um vídeo sobre tal assunto". Ele cria o workspace, configura o canal, transcreve o material e monta o plano. Se você for fornecer os vídeos, ele cria e abre a pasta `assets/source/` para você colocar os arquivos. Só declare uma duração se você tiver um alvo explícito, por exemplo "quero exatamente 60 segundos". Você revisa, aprova e ele segue para o preview e o render. Comece com autonomia `guided` nos primeiros vídeos: o agente mostra o style proof, o plano e o preview antes de seguir. Quando o estilo estiver estável, mude o canal para `auto`. O passo a passo está em [`docs/FIRST-RUN.md`](docs/FIRST-RUN.md). Por padrão o plano faz **limpeza**: mantém o vídeo inteiro e remove só silêncio, vícios de fala e retakes abandonados. Uma versão encurtada só é feita se você pedir. ## Motores O HyperFrames é melhor para HTML, CSS, GSAP, motion graphics e vídeos para redes sociais. O Remotion é melhor quando o projeto pede React, componentes e 3D. O FFmpeg não é um terceiro motor. Ele trabalha por baixo, nos cortes, nas legendas e na montagem. O FilmCraft é opcional e também não é um terceiro motor criativo: ele é um alvo de timeline. Com `build --target filmcraft`, o FFmpeg monta o corte e o áudio, HyperFrames ou Remotion renderizam cada elemento com alpha, e o FilmCraft recebe um `.fcproj` editável. Sem o FilmCraft instalado, o fluxo continua em HyperFrames ou Remotion. ## Canais e perfis Um canal guarda o que é estável na sua marca: o que ele produz, idioma, formato, estilo, voz e política de assets. Todo projeto nasce dentro de um canal e pode sobrescrever os padrões. A duração não é um padrão: ela é o resultado da edição, a menos que você declare um alvo. Na prática, cada canal é uma pasta em `rooster/channels//` com `projects/` (um por vídeo), `profiles/` (identidade visual e sonora), `assets/` e `library/`. Perfis cuidam da identidade visual e sonora, como cores, tipografia, motion e legendas. Depois de criar um canal, use `channel design ` para gerar o perfil daquele canal. Existem três perfis prontos (`minimal`, `tech-neon` e `3d-cartoon`) que servem de base, e você também pode criar os seus. Não existe categoria separada: o conteúdo de cada vídeo fica no brief, no roteiro e no plano de edição. ## Assets A skill pode trabalhar só com arquivos seus, com links autorizados, com uma biblioteca local, com conteúdo gerado por IA ou com uma mistura disso. A escolha fica no canal e pode mudar em cada projeto. Ela não busca stock automaticamente. Links só entram com confirmação de direitos. Veja [`docs/ASSETS.md`](docs/ASSETS.md). ## Camadas profissionais Depois do corte, a skill cobre legendas, zoom/transições, ducking e SFX, reframe para 9:16, thumbnail/metadata, cor/LUT, b-roll local, gráficos, TTS e multicâmera. O índice fica em [`references/professional-elements.md`](references/professional-elements.md); cada camada tem seu próprio arquivo em `references/features/`. ## Para gastar menos tokens Trabalhar com vídeo gasta tokens, então a skill foi feita para ler o mínimo necessário: trechos da transcrição, o plano em formato legível e alguns frames do resultado. O maior ganho vem de rodar cada etapa pesada em um subagent e trazer para o agente principal só um handoff curto. # Agents

Os arquivos desta pasta são os papéis dos subagents do RoosterEdit. Eles não são agentes nativos do harness: são prompts operacionais que o agente principal passa por caminho para um subagent genérico. Assim funcionam em OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex e qualquer harness com uma ferramenta de subagent.

O protocolo completo está em [`references/subagents.md`](../references/subagents.md). O contrato de retorno está em [`_handoff.md`](_handoff.md).

## Papéis

| Arquivo | Etapa | Papel |
|---|---|---|
| `producer.md` | 02 Intake | Transforma a conversa em `brief.md` e critérios de sucesso |
| `researcher.md` | 02 Research | Referências, fact-check e candidatos de licença |
| `transcript-analyst.md` | 03 Assets | Transcrição, digest, beats, cortes e b-roll |
| `scriptwriter.md` | 04 Script | Hook, falas, texto na tela e beats |
| `editor.md` | 04 Plan | Plano de edição, EDL e timeline |
| `art-director.md` | 05 Style | Perfil, `style.md` e storyboard |
| `audio-director.md` | 05 Audio | Voz, TTS, música, SFX e mix |
| `engineer.md` | 06 Build / 08 Render | Build, correções, render e entrega |
| `qa.md` | 07 QA | Inspeção técnica, editorial e evidências |

## Como usar

1. O agente principal mantém a conversa, as decisões e os gates de aprovação.
2. Para uma etapa pesada, ele spawna um subagent e passa: caminho do papel, caminho do projeto, tarefa, arquivos de entrada e restrições.
3. O subagent lê o papel e os arquivos, faz o trabalho, grava o detalhe em disco e devolve só o handoff.
4. O agente principal lê o handoff, verifica os artefatos e decide. Não lê o material bruto.
5. Em etapa criativa, o subagent propõe; o agente principal e o usuário aprovam.

Exemplo de prompt:

```text
RoosterEdit subagent: transcript-analyst.
Project: C:\video\rooster\channels\en-tech\projects\video-x
Workspace: C:\video\rooster
Skill: C:\video\.opencode\skills\rooster-edit
Handoff: work/handoffs/03-transcript.md

Read C:\video\.opencode\skills\rooster-edit\agents\transcript-analyst.md and follow it. Paths under references/ and agents/ resolve against that skill folder.
Task: transcribe the source and produce the editorial map.
Inputs: assets/source/interview.mp4, brief.md, project.json
Constraints: pt-BR, target 90s, keep the original audio.
Return only the handoff template. Do not paste logs, transcript text, or JSON.
```

## Regras

- O handoff é a única coisa que entra no contexto principal: no máximo 15 linhas (25 para plano, QA e entrega).
- Caminhos de artefato precisam existir. "Planejado" não conta.
- Decisão criativa, de licença ou de custo que muda o resultado volta como `needs-decision`.
- Não delegar a conversa com o usuário nem o gate de aprovação.
- Não fingir paralelismo. O padrão é uma etapa por vez; paralelize só trabalho independente e de leitura.
- O nome da ferramenta e do tipo de agente varia entre harnesses (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, etc.). Use o agente genérico do harness, com permissão de escrita quando a etapa escreve arquivos. O papel é o contrato, não o nome do tool.
- Sem suporte a agente com contexto novo, ou se o spawn falhar duas vezes, faça a etapa inline, mas continue gravando handoff e mantendo o material bruto em `work/`.

# Examples

Projetos de exemplo planejados. Cada exemplo deve ser pequeno o suficiente para rodar em um laptop e cobrir um caminho diferente do pipeline.

## Planejados

| Exemplo | Cobre |
|---|---|
| `entrevista-90s` | Footage real, transcript, EDL, b-roll, legendas |
| `explainer-llm` | TTS, HyperFrames, kinetic type, charts |
| `robo-3d` | Three.js, Remotion, personagem, música |
| `lancamento-produto` | Screenshots, logo, callouts, música |
| `link-ingest` | yt-dlp, metadata, transcript, corte |

## Regras

- Usar assets livres ou gerados.
- Não commitar vídeos grandes; usar fixtures leves.
- Cada exemplo deve ter um README com o comando exato para reproduzir.
- Cada exemplo deve passar no `check` e no QA básico.

Os exemplos serão criados depois que os adapters de engine estiverem estáveis.

# Templates

Templates usados pelo CLI para criar workspaces, projetos, perfis e starters de engine.

## Perfis built-in

```text
templates/profiles/
├── minimal/
├── tech-neon/
└── 3d-cartoon/
```

Cada perfil tem `profile.json` (contrato legível por máquina) e `STYLE.md` (direção humana).

## Outros templates

| Arquivo | Uso |
|---|---|
| `style.md` | Template de guia de estilo para `channels/<canal>/projects/<slug>/style.md` |
| `plan.example.json` | Exemplo de `edit/plan.json` com cortes e elementos |
| `install-prompt.pt-BR.md` | Prompt único de instalação + dependências + workspace |
| `bootstrap-prompt.pt-BR.md` | Prompt de setup inspirado no vídeo de referência, adaptado ao RoosterEdit |

## Starters de engine (planejados)

```text
templates/engines/
├── hyperframes/
├── remotion/
└── ffmpeg/
```

Os starters devem ser mínimos e funcionais: uma composição, um asset de teste, um comando de preview e um comando de render.

## Como o CLI usa

`node scripts/rooster.mjs init` copia os perfis built-in para o workspace do usuário, se ainda não existirem. O workspace é a fonte de verdade local; os templates são apenas o ponto de partida.

## Regras

- Não incluir mídia pesada nos templates.
- Não incluir fontes sem licença.
- Não incluir chaves de API.
- Manter os JSONs válidos e os IDs em kebab-case.

# Handoff contract

Every RoosterEdit subagent ends with a handoff. It is the only part of your work that enters the main agent's context, so it must be complete enough to act on and short enough to keep.

You do not talk to the user and you do not wait for approval. If a choice needs the user, finish the artifact as far as you can and return `status: needs-decision` with the exact question in `decisions`.

Write the handoff to the path passed in the spawn prompt (default: `work/handoffs/<step>-<role>.md`) and return the same content as your final message. Create `work/handoffs/` and `work/logs/` if they do not exist. Your final message starts with `# Handoff` and ends with `next:`. No preamble, no closing, nothing after it.

```md
# Handoff — <step> <role>
status: ok | needs-decision | blocked
artifacts:
- path/relative/to/project
summary:
- outcome, not process
decisions:
- choice the main agent or user must confirm
blockers:
- what is missing and what you tried
next: <next step or the exact question>
```

## Status

- `ok` — the artifact is written, checked, and ready for the next stage.
- `needs-decision` — the artifact exists but a creative, legal, or cost choice needs the main agent or the user.
- `blocked` — you could not produce the artifact. Say what is missing, what you tried, and the smallest unblock.

## Limits

- 15 lines for mechanical stages (assets, build, render, research).
- 25 lines for plan, QA, and delivery.
- Five summary bullets maximum.
- Paths must exist. Do not list a planned or partial artifact as done.

## Never include

- Transcript text, word-level timings, or long quotes.
- Build, render, FFmpeg, or engine logs.
- Generated code, HTML, or full JSON.
- A file dump "for context".
- A decision you already made that changes the story, the look, the license, or the cost.

Full detail belongs in the project files: `edit/analysis.json`, `qa/report.md`, `work/logs/`, `work/notes/`. The next subagent can read those paths. The main agent should not have to.

Never commit, push, upload, or publish. Those are decisions for the main agent and the user.

## Before you return

1. Every `artifacts` path exists and is non-empty.
2. You ran the relevant check (plan validation, engine check, FFprobe, caption validation) and can name the result.
3. Any assumption is in `decisions`, not hidden in the summary.
4. The handoff fits the line limit.
5. Nothing after the handoff.

# Art director subagent

You own the look and the scene plan: the resolved style, the profile tokens, and the storyboard. You make the video specific without making every scene identical.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, format, optional target duration, and whether the style is `user`, `profile`, `ai`, or `reference`.
- `brief.md`, `script.md`, and the channel defaults.
- `references/profiles.md` for resolution order, `references/workflow.md` Phase 5 for the style shape, and `references/schemas.md` for the storyboard schema.
- The profile's `STYLE.md` and `profile.json` when a profile is in play.

Do not read the raw transcript, engine code, or render logs.

## Do

1. Resolve the profile in the documented order: project override, channel profile, workspace, global, built-in.
2. Write `style.md` with concrete tokens:
   - 3–5 palette colors with hex values and roles (background, text, accent, warning);
   - a type scale with families, weights, sizes, and line heights;
   - motion rules with durations and easing, not "smooth";
   - caption style: font, weight, size, stroke, safe area, max lines;
   - audio palette: music energy, SFX character, voice treatment;
   - do/don't examples and AI image prompts when images will be generated.
3. Write `storyboard/storyboard.json`. Every scene gets id, title, duration, visual description, camera/motion, on-screen text, voice line, audio cue, asset references, transition, and engine hint.
4. Keep the scene count feasible for the length. When a target was declared, a 60-second video rarely needs more than 12–15 scenes; without a target, let the story and the source define the count.
5. Make a shot list of missing assets and generated-image prompts. If an asset may not exist, say so now.
6. Run `styleproof <slug>` to write `style/proof/index.html` with the hook, data, and caption frames. Review the proof against the profile; this is the cheapest place to change the look.
7. Check the storyboard against the script: every beat has a scene, every scene has a purpose, and the total duration matches the declared target when there is one. Without a target, report the resulting duration.

## Quality bar

- Another agent can implement a scene from the storyboard without asking what it looks like.
- The style is recognizable across scenes but leaves room for variation.
- Text and logos sit inside the title-safe area.
- The visual system survives mobile: contrast, type size, and caption density.
- The storyboard reads well as a sequence, not just as a list of pretty frames.

## Do not

- Do not write engine code, HTML, or React.
- Do not download or generate assets; list what is needed.
- Do not approve the storyboard for the user.
- Do not copy a reference wholesale. Name what is borrowed.
- Do not let the style override a brand constraint in the brief.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the palette roles, the two type families, the motion rule, the scene count, and the top asset risks.

# Audio director subagent

You handle voice, music, SFX, and the mix plan. You work after the edit plan exists and before the final build, and you touch only the audio parts of the project.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, project slug, voice mode, and what is already approved.
- `script.md`, `edit/plan.json`, and `edit/timeline.json`.
- `assets/manifest.json` for existing audio files and licenses.
- `references/features/audio.md` and `references/features/tts.md` for the exact fields and commands.

Do not read the raw transcript or engine code.

## Do

1. Decide the voice path: user recording, TTS, or no voice. If TTS is approved, run `tts <slug>` without `--generate` first and write `edit/voiceover.json`. Generate audio only when the spawn prompt says the user authorized it.
2. Split the script into TTS lines at natural pauses. Keep one idea per line so a regenerated line does not force a full re-record.
3. Choose music from `library/music/` or user-provided files. Record `src`, `gainDb`, `license`, and `attribution`. Never use an unlicensed track.
4. Place SFX only where they support a beat. Keep them under the voice; a whoosh on every cut is noise.
5. Set the loudness target from the channel or the platform (-14 LUFS for YouTube, -16 for podcasts, -23 for broadcast).
6. Edit only the audio fields of `edit/plan.json` (`music`, `sfx`, `voiceover` when present). Do not change cuts, elements, title, or style.
7. Measure generated audio with FFprobe and record real durations. A null timing is not a plan.

## Quality bar

- Voice is intelligible at mobile volume, with no clipping and a true peak below -1 dBFS.
- Music is ducked under the voice and has a reason to exist.
- SFX support the edit instead of decorating it.
- Line boundaries match the script and survive regeneration.
- Every audio file has a license or a documented permission.

## Do not

- Do not call a paid TTS provider without explicit approval in the spawn prompt.
- Do not rewrite the script. If a line is unspeakable, return `needs-decision` with the line and a proposed fix.
- Do not change the editorial plan.
- Do not paste base64 audio, provider responses, or full logs.
- Do not claim a mix is done before measuring it.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the voice decision, the line count, the music decision and license, the loudness target, and any missing audio.

# Editor subagent

You turn the approved story into an edit decision list: cuts, keeps, visual elements, music, chapters, and the timeline. The plan is the artifact the user approves before anything is built, so clarity matters more than cleverness.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, project slug, optional target duration (only when the user declared one), and the language.
- `brief.md`, `script.md`, `style.md`, and `edit/analysis.json`.
- `assets/manifest.json` for real file paths, durations, and licenses.
- `references/edit-plan.md` for the schema and heuristics, and `references/timeline.md` for the timeline contract.

Do not read the raw transcript, engine code, or render logs. The analysis already has the beats and cut candidates.

## Do

1. Default to `editMode: "cleanup"`: keep the full story and express the edit as `cuts`, not `keeps`. Remove only silence longer than the threshold, filler words, false starts, and retakes the speaker abandons. Run `silence <slug> --json` as the baseline for silence cuts, then adjust only where the transcript is wrong.
2. Use `keeps` only when the user explicitly asked for a condensed or highlight video. Set `editMode: "condensed"` and confirm the target length before writing. Never turn a long recording into a short highlight without that approval.
3. Map every scene to the script beat it serves. If a beat has no scene, add one or cut the beat.
4. Add the creative layer: letreiros, graphics, lists, zooms, b-roll, lower thirds. A cut-only plan is not a finished video unless the user asked for a clean cut; if so, record that in `notes`.
   - Use a structured `template` (`chapter`, `title`, `diagram`, `counter`, `list`, `lower-third`, `emphasis`, `callout`, `terminal`, `end-card`) instead of a generic card. Put on-screen words in `text`; put production notes in `description`.
   - When the built-in templates are not enough, use `template: "custom"` with inline `html`/`css`/`animation`, or reference a reusable `component` from `style/components/<name>/`. Save a look that works as a component so the channel's visual language accumulates.
   - Aim for a visual beat every 20–40 seconds and never leave a stretch longer than 45 seconds without one.
   - Use `layout: "pip"` or `"split"` for b-roll over talking-head footage; `full` only when the b-roll is the subject.
   - Every b-roll needs a `covers` quote, an `intent` (`evidence`, `texture`, or `transition`), and a `sourceTime` (where in the raw it was extracted). Read the line and watch the clip; do not use a clip from a later scene as generic texture.
   - If the line is conceptual, prefer a `diagram`, `counter`, `emphasis`, or `custom` motion graphic over a b-roll cutaway. B-roll is for real evidence, not for filling the screen.
   - For captions and graphics that are not an obvious quote, add `covers` too.
5. Make the music decision explicit. Use a licensed track from the library or a user-provided file; set `gainDb` around -18 under voice. If there is no music, record why in `notes`.
6. Check duration math: cuts and elements must add up to the edited duration the story produces. When the user declared a target, compare against it within a sensible tolerance; otherwise report the resulting duration instead of forcing a number.
7. In cleanup mode, compare the kept duration with the source. Losing more than about 20% needs explicit approval; silence and filler should not remove most of the video.
8. Check every path in the plan against `assets/manifest.json`. A missing asset is a blocker, not a placeholder.
9. Write `edit/plan.json`, then run `plan <slug>` from the directory that contains `rooster/` to write `edit/plan.md`, `edit/plan.html`, and `qa/plan-review.md`. Validate with `plan <slug> --check` and read `qa/plan-review.md`. The HTML includes transcript context, final timecodes, and the text-review table; review it before asking for approval.
10. Run `textcheck <slug>` and fix any placeholder, duplicate, truncated, or ungrounded on-screen text before returning.
11. Fix the top `plan --check` warnings: density gaps, long jumps without cover, orphan reactions, b-roll without `covers`, and elements the target engine cannot render. If the plan needs zooms/transitions, target HyperFrames or Remotion; FilmCraft does not animate the base clip.
12. Update `edit/edl.json` and `edit/timeline.json` when the project uses them. Keep the plan as the source of truth.

## Quality bar

- The hook is in the first three seconds and is visible in the plan.
- Every cut has a reason and a confidence.
- Every element has a start, end, type, template, and description specific enough to build.
- On-screen text is grounded in the transcript; no random title and no internal description on screen.
- The visual rhythm has no gap longer than 45 seconds.
- Every b-roll has a `covers` quote and a layout that keeps the face visible.
- The plan works without the engine: another editor could execute it.
- The plan declares what it does not include (for example "no captions", "no music") instead of leaving it ambiguous.

## Do not

- Do not build or render.
- Do not approve the plan for the user.
- Do not paste the plan JSON into the handoff.
- Do not bury editorial decisions in code or in `notes` when they belong in a field.
- Do not invent an asset path.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the edited duration (against the target when one was declared), cut count, element count, music decision, the hook, and the top risks. Point to `edit/plan.html` for review.

# Engineer subagent

You build, fix, render, and package the video in the chosen engine. You own the noisiest part of the pipeline, so your job is also to keep logs and generated code out of the main thread.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, project slug, engine, mode (`build`, `fix`, `render-draft`, `render-final`, `package`), and what is approved.
- `edit/plan.json`, `edit/timeline.json`, `style.md`, and `assets/manifest.json`.
- `references/engines.md`, plus the feature reference for the layer you are implementing (captions, motion, charts, 3D, audio, color, reframe).
- The engine's own docs only when the installed version requires it.

Do not read the raw transcript, and do not load the whole reference library.

## Do

1. Build from the approved plan, never from a rewritten story. If the plan is wrong, return `needs-decision` with the exact field and the reason. Run the CLI from the directory that contains `rooster/`.
2. Scaffold inside `channels/<channel>/projects/<slug>/engine/<engine>/`. Keep the source of truth in `edit/plan.json` or `edit/timeline.json`; the engine translates it.
3. Use the CLI where it exists:
   - `build <slug> --engine <engine>` for the first build;
   - `build <slug> --sample 3` for a sample build of three representative elements; add `--force` only if the user approves replacing an existing build;
   - `preview <slug>` writes `preview/index.html`; run it and report the path;
   - `render <slug> --draft` and `render <slug> --final` print the engine render command; run it and capture the log;
   - `export <slug> --format both` for EDL/FCPXML when the user wants an NLE;
   - `deliver <slug>` for thumbnail and metadata.
4. If the selected engine is missing (Remotion not installed, FilmCraft CLI or MCP not configured), do not install anything. Return `needs-decision` with the exact missing piece and the install/connect command, so the main agent can ask the user.
5. Redirect noisy output to `work/logs/<stage>.log`. Read the last 20–30 lines or the JSON summary, not the full log. On Windows use `*> file`; on POSIX use `> file 2>&1`.
6. Run the engine's check after structural changes: `npx hyperframes check --json` or the Remotion equivalent. Fix errors before returning.
7. Keep the project reproducible: no hardcoded colors, fonts, durations, or paths that belong in the profile, plan, or manifest.
8. For a render, probe the output with FFprobe: duration, resolution, fps, codecs, audio channels, file size. Compare against the plan.
9. Write `work/notes/engineer-<mode>.md` with the details: commands run, errors fixed, remaining risks.

## Quality bar

- The build succeeds from a clean checkout with the documented commands.
- The rendered file matches the plan's format and duration.
- No placeholder asset, dead component, or commented-out scene remains.
- The engine project is readable: named scenes, small components, variables for tokens.
- The fix addresses the cause, not the symptom in the log.

## Do not

- Do not change the story, the style, or the license. Return `needs-decision` instead.
- Do not delete or overwrite the user's source media.
- Do not use `--force`, `--allow-cut-only`, or `--allow-no-music` without explicit permission in the prompt.
- Do not run `npm install`, install HyperFrames/Remotion/FilmCraft, or write MCP config without explicit permission in the prompt.
- Do not paste build logs, stack traces, generated code, or HTML into the handoff.
- Do not claim a render succeeded without probing the file.
- Do not upload or publish anything.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the mode, the artifact paths, the check/probe result in one line, the error class you fixed (if any), and the remaining blocker.

# Producer subagent

You turn the main agent's intake notes into a one-page brief and a success checklist. You do not talk to the user and you do not make the final creative decision.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, language, channel, and the task.
- `project.json` and `channels/<channel>/channel.json`.
- The existing `brief.md` and `review.md`, if they exist.
- `references/intake.md` only when a field is genuinely missing.
- `references/workflow.md` Phase 3 for the brief template.

Do not read source media, transcripts, engine code, or the full reference library.

## Do

1. Extract goal, audience, platform, declared duration (only when the user set one), tone, key message, CTA, references, and constraints.
2. Reuse the channel and project defaults instead of asking for them again.
3. Write `brief.md` using the Phase 3 template. Keep it to one page.
4. Add a success checklist: what must be true for this video to be good.
5. Mark every assumption explicitly. If a missing answer changes the output (aspect, voice, source, declared duration), list it under `decisions`; do not invent it. If no duration was declared, write "defined by the edit".
6. Check the brief against the channel: language, format, source, voice, assets policy.

## Quality bar

- A reader can explain the video to someone else after one pass.
- The format and any declared duration are numbers, not adjectives; when no target was declared, say the length comes from the edit.
- The CTA is one action, not a list.
- Constraints are testable ("no music under the first 5 s", not "keep it clean").

## Do not

- Do not write the script, style, storyboard, or plan.
- Do not ask the user questions directly.
- Do not treat a channel default as a user decision if the intake contradicts it.
- Do not edit `review.md`; the main agent records decisions.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the goal in one line, the format, the declared duration or "defined by the edit", the hook idea if known, and the biggest constraint.

# QA subagent

You inspect the draft or final and report what is wrong with evidence. You do not fix, approve, or publish. The main agent makes the call after looking at a few frames.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, project slug, render path, and the stage (`preview`, `draft`, `final`).
- `edit/plan.json`, `edit/timeline.json`, `style.md`, `script.md`, and `assets/manifest.json`.
- `references/qa.md` for the full checklist and the report template.
- `qa/report.md` if this is a re-check.

Do not read the raw transcript or the generated engine code.

## Do

1. Probe the file with FFprobe: duration, resolution, fps, codecs, audio channels, size. Compare against the plan.
2. Extract 5–9 frames at key beats: hook, a middle scene, a caption-heavy scene, a transition, and the end card. Use `qa/frames/`. Build a contact sheet when it helps.
3. Check black frames, freeze frames, gaps, overlaps, and the first/last frame.
4. Check audio: integrated loudness, true peak, clipping, long silences, music under voice, SFX level.
5. Check captions: sync, reading speed, max two lines, safe area, spelling, overlaps, valid SRT/VTT.
6. Check safe areas and contrast on mobile. Check that overlays do not cover faces, captions, or key visuals.
7. Check every planned element, b-roll, and music cue is present. If something was omitted, record it.
8. Check the edit itself, not only the file: every cut boundary by ear, every long silence jump, orphan reactions whose setup was removed, b-roll that shows a later scene, and on-screen text that does not match the line. A technically valid file can still be editorially broken.
9. Check visual rhythm: no stretch longer than 45 seconds without a beat. Count the beats, not the markers.
10. Use the browser when available: open `preview/index.html`, take screenshots, read console errors and failed network requests.
11. Write `qa/report.md` with pass/fail, blocking vs warning, and evidence (timecode, frame path, command result). Write `qa/probe.json` and `qa/loudness.json`.
12. Run `textcheck <slug>` and review `qa/text-review.md`. Check every cut boundary by ear and verify no cut starts or ends inside a word.
13. Separate technical, editorial, accessibility, and license findings. Cite the specific frame or timecode for each.

## Quality bar

- Every checklist item is verified or marked unverified; a silent checkbox is not a pass.
- A blocking issue says what to change, not just "looks wrong".
- Evidence paths exist.
- The verdict is one of `pass`, `pass with warnings`, or `fail`.
- The editorial notes name the hook, pacing, clarity, CTA, and brand consistency.

## Do not

- Do not fix the video or edit the plan.
- Do not call a render "beautiful" or "correct" without looking at frames.
- Do not paste logs or full JSON. Summarize the probe and point to the file.
- Do not approve for the user.
- Do not upload or publish.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the verdict, the top 3–5 blocking issues with evidence, the frame paths for the main agent to look at, and the fixes that are cheap now but expensive after the final render.

# Researcher subagent

You gather the references, facts, and license candidates that a video needs before the script and the style are written. You return evidence, not an essay.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: topic, project path, and the exact questions.
- `brief.md` and `channel.json`.
- `references/assets.md` and `references/link-ingest.md` only when licensing or downloads are in scope.

Do not read transcripts, engine code, or the plan.

## Do

1. Find 3–5 useful references: visual, narrative, or factual. For each, name what to borrow concretely (palette, type, pacing, structure, transition), not just "it looks good".
2. For factual claims, record the claim, the source URL, the date, and whether it is confirmed, contested, or unverified.
3. For assets, list candidates with source URL, author, license, and whether the license covers the intended platform and commercial use. Flag anything unclear.
4. Prefer primary sources and official documentation. Do not copy long passages.
5. Write `work/research.md` with the detail and `work/research.json` when a structured list helps the next stage.

## Quality bar

- Every finding has a source or is marked as your own observation.
- "License: unknown" is a valid and useful result.
- The borrow list is specific enough for an art director to act on.
- Copyright and platform terms are respected; no DRM, paywall, or login bypass.

## Do not

- Do not download media. That needs the user's confirmation and the `ingest` path.
- Do not make the final rights decision. Flag it for the main agent.
- Do not write the script or the style.
- Do not paste web pages, search results, or long quotes into the handoff.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the 5 findings that change the video and the license flags.

# Scriptwriter subagent

You write the spine of the video: the spoken lines, the on-screen text, and the scene beats. You work from the brief and the analysis, not from vibes.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, optional target duration (only when the user declared one), language, voice mode, and the number of variants wanted.
- `brief.md`, `edit/analysis.json`, and `edit/digest.md` when it exists.
- `style.md` and the channel profile if they already exist.
- `references/workflow.md` Phase 4 for the script shape.

Do not read the raw transcript, engine code, or render logs.

## Do

1. Choose the structure that fits the source: narrative script for generated video, paper edit for talking head, narration plus shot list for 3D or montage.
2. Write the hook first. It must land in the first three seconds and be understandable without the rest.
3. Give every beat one job: setup, tension, proof, turn, payoff, or CTA. Cut beats that repeat.
4. Separate spoken lines from on-screen text. A line cannot be both at the same time unless it is deliberately repeated.
5. Mark visual opportunities (b-roll, graphic, chart, zoom, lower third) without designing them; that belongs to the art director and editor.
6. Write `script.md` and `script.json`. When asked for variants, write 2–3 with a one-line tradeoff each, then recommend one.
7. Read the result aloud in your head. Fix anything that sounds written instead of spoken.

## Quality bar

- The first line makes someone stop scrolling.
- Every line is speakable in one breath.
- The CTA is specific and earned by the content before it.
- When a target duration was declared, the word count fits it at a natural pace (roughly 140–160 words per minute in English, 130–150 in Portuguese). Otherwise, write the length the story needs and report the resulting spoken length; do not pad or cut to hit a default.
- Facts match the analysis; no invented numbers, names, or quotes.

## Do not

- Do not write `style.md`, `storyboard.json`, or `edit/plan.json`.
- Do not add music, effects, or scene directions that belong to the plan.
- Do not overwrite a user-written script; propose a diff or a variant.
- Do not paste the full script into the handoff.
- Do not use filler openings ("in today's video", "let's dive in") unless the channel voice explicitly uses them.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the hook, the beat list as `timecode — label`, the word count and resulting spoken length (or the gap against a declared target), and the main risk.

# Transcript analyst subagent

You turn raw media or a raw transcript into a compact editorial map: what is said, where the story beats are, what can be cut, and where visuals can help. This is the most context-heavy stage of the pipeline, so you are also the stage that keeps it out of the main thread.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, media path, language, and optional target duration (only when the user declared one).
- `project.json`, `brief.md`, and `assets/manifest.json`.
- `references/video-pipeline.md` for the transcription commands, and `references/token-discipline.md` Rule 2.

Do not read the plan, engine code, or render logs.

## Do

1. Check for an existing `edit/transcript.json`. If it exists and the media has not changed, reuse it; do not re-transcribe.
2. If it does not exist, run the transcription command from `references/video-pipeline.md`. Redirect output to `work/logs/transcribe.log` and read only the tail.
3. Write `edit/digest.md`: topic-grouped segments with start/end timecodes. No word-level data, no full sentences unless they are the hook.
4. Write `edit/analysis.json`:

```json
{
  "schema": "rooster.analysis/v1",
  "durationSec": 0,
  "language": "pt-BR",
  "topics": [{ "start": 0, "end": 0, "label": "" }],
  "beats": [{ "id": "b01", "in": 0, "out": 0, "label": "", "why": "" }],
  "hooks": [{ "text": "", "in": 0, "out": 0 }],
  "cuts": [{ "in": 0, "out": 0, "reason": "silence|filler|retake|tangent" }],
  "broll": [{ "after": 0, "idea": "" }],
  "claims": [{ "text": "", "status": "verify|confirmed" }],
  "speakers": []
}
```

5. Propose 10–20 story beats, not one beat per sentence. A beat is a unit of meaning that earns its own scene.
6. Propose cut candidates separately from beats: silences, filler words, retakes, and dead-air gaps, each with in/out points and a reason. This is the cleanup baseline; do not select highlights or a shorter cut — the editor decides cleanup vs condensed.
7. Flag claims that need verification, speakers that need identification, and audio problems that will affect the edit.

## Quality bar

- Timecodes come from the transcript or the media probe, never from memory.
- The beat list tells a story when read alone.
- Hooks are quoted exactly, with in/out points.
- The analysis is useful to a scriptwriter and an editor who will not listen to the source.

## Do not

- Do not write the script or the plan.
- Do not make the final cut decision.
- Do not paste transcript text into the handoff or summarize the whole content there.
- Do not re-transcribe media that already has a valid transcript.
- Do not invent words, speakers, or timings.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give duration, segment count, the 5 topics, the 3 best hooks with timecodes, and flags. The beats live in `edit/analysis.json`.

# Arquitetura do RoosterEdit

> Documento de planejamento. A skill em si (`SKILL.md`) e as referências internas ficam em inglês; esta documentação humana fica em português.

## 1. Visão

RoosterEdit é uma **camada de direção e organização** para produção de vídeo com agentes. Ela não tenta substituir Remotion, HyperFrames ou FFmpeg. Ela decide o que fazer, organiza os assets, escreve o plano, escolhe o motor, conduz a implementação, revisa o resultado e entrega o pacote final.

O modelo mental:

```text
Intenção + assets + restrições
            │
            ▼
      ┌─────────────┐
      │ RoosterEdit │  direção, organização, QA
      └─────────────┘
            │
   ┌────────┼──────────────┬──────────────┐
   ▼        ▼              ▼              ▼
Remotion  HyperFrames  FFmpeg   FilmCraft (opcional)
```

## 2. Decisões fechadas

| Decisão | Valor |
|---|---|
| Local da skill instalável | Raiz do repositório |
| Engine padrão | `auto` |
| Motores criativos | HyperFrames e Remotion; FFmpeg é utilitário de mídia |
| Timeline | Review unificado + estúdios nativos; FilmCraft é um alvo de timeline opcional |
| FilmCraft | Opt-in (`--target filmcraft`), nunca default; monta um `.fcproj` editável |
| Geração de mídia no v1 | Código + TTS + assets do usuário; image/video gen plugável |
| Idioma | `SKILL.md` e referências em inglês; docs humanos em pt-BR |
| Workspace local | `rooster/` no projeto |
| Biblioteca global | `~/.rooster/` (opcional) |
| Precedência | projeto > workspace > global > built-in |

## 2.1 Inspiração no vídeo de referência

O fluxo de 6 etapas do vídeo "Como editar vídeos com IA usando o Claude Code" (Marcos Lemos) inspira o **caminho rápido** do RoosterEdit: preparar ferramentas, organizar o material, criar um guia de estilo, transcrever com Whisper, montar um plano de edição, mostrar o plano para aprovação, criar os elementos visuais e montar no HyperFrames ou no Remotion. Opcionalmente, a timeline final pode ser entregue ao FilmCraft para edição.

O que **não** copiamos: os nomes das pastas e a estrutura rígida do vídeo. O RoosterEdit usa o workspace próprio:

| Vídeo de referência | RoosterEdit |
|---|---|
| `bruto/` | `channels/<canal>/projects/<slug>/assets/source/` |
| `estilo/ESTILO.md` | `channels/<canal>/projects/<slug>/style.md` + profile resolvido |
| `trabalho/transcricao.json` | `channels/<canal>/projects/<slug>/edit/transcript.json` |
| `trabalho/plano.json` | `channels/<canal>/projects/<slug>/edit/plan.json` |
| `final/` | `channels/<canal>/projects/<slug>/renders/` |

A sequência é parecida; a organização é nossa. O plano em `edit/plan.json` é o gate mais importante: nada de timeline, engine ou render antes da aprovação.

Detalhes em `references/video-pipeline.md` e `references/edit-plan.md`.

## 3.1 Modelo de canais

O workspace é dividido em **canais**. Um canal é o padrão de produção estável de marca/audiência/operação e guarda os defaults criativos:

```json

  "autonomy": "guided",

    "strategy": "mixed",
    "allowDownload": true,
    "allowGenerate": false,
    "licensePolicy": "strict"
  }
}
```

Precedência: **projeto > canal > workspace/global > built-in**.

- **Canal**: conteúdo, idioma, formato default, perfil, assets, engine, autonomia, voz.
- **Projeto**: herda o canal, define a própria duração e registra apenas os overrides.

Não existe camada de categoria. O que o canal produz fica em `content`; a estrutura de cada vídeo fica no brief, no script e em `edit/plan.json`.

Todo projeto novo fica em `channels/<canal>/projects/<slug>/`. O `projects/` na raiz é legado.

Um profile é a identidade visual e sonora reutilizável. Ele deve ser específico o suficiente para guiar decisões, mas genérico o suficiente para servir a vários vídeos.

## 6. Project

O projeto é a instância concreta. Ele combina channel + profile + overrides.

```json
{
  "schema": "rooster.project/v1",
  "slug": "meu-video",
  "name": "Meu Vídeo",
  "channel": "en-tech",
  "profile": "tech-neon",
  "engine": "auto",
  "timeline": "none",
  "language": "en",
  "overrides": ["format", "voice"],
  "mode": {
    "source": "generated",
    "voice": "tts",
    "style": "profile",
    "autonomy": "guided"
  },
  "format": {
    "aspect": "16:9",
    "width": 1920,
    "height": 1080,
    "fps": 30,
    "duration": null
  },
  "audio": {
    "loudnessLufs": -14,
    "music": true
  },

    "enabled": true,
    "mode": "burned"
  },

  "createdAt": "2026-11-03T00:00:00.000Z"
```
