# Assets

Assets are the raw material of the project. This reference explains the supported strategies, the folder contract, and how the user can change the source of truth.

## Strategies

| Strategy | Meaning | Current support |
|---|---|---|
| `user` | Only files the user provides | Yes (`ingest --file`) |
| `link` | Authorized URLs downloaded by the agent | Yes for video links via `yt-dlp`; direct image URLs are not robust yet |
| `library` | Workspace/global music, SFX, fonts, overlays, b-roll | Folders exist; no catalog UI yet |
| `generated` | AI-generated images, TTS, video, etc. | TTS can be delegated to HyperFrames/media-use or a provider; image/video generation is pluggable, not built in |
| `none` | No external assets | Yes; text/motion graphics only |
| `mixed` | All of the above, with permission | Yes, with explicit consent |

The strategy lives in the channel (`channels/<id>/channel.json`), with a workspace fallback in `rooster/config.json` and a project override in `project.json`:

```json
{
  "assets": {
    "strategy": "mixed",
    "allowDownload": true,
    "allowGenerate": false,
    "licensePolicy": "strict"
  }
}
```

A project can override it in `project.json`:

```json
{
  "assets": {
    "strategy": "user",
    "sources": ["user"],
    "licensePolicy": "strict"
  }
}
```

## Folder contract

```text
channels/<canal>/projects/<slug>/assets/
├── source/       files from the user
├── generated/    AI-generated images, audio, video
├── licensed/     stock, music, fonts, overlays with a recorded license
└── manifest.json inventory, hashes, probe data, license, provenance
```

The agent must never delete or overwrite the user's originals. Prefer copying or hard-linking into the project. The original stays where the user put it.

## Manifest

Every asset gets an entry with:

- stable id and relative path;
- type (`video`, `audio`, `image`, `font`, `other`);
- hash, bytes, and probe data;
- source (`user`, `url`, `generated`, `stock`, `library`);
- license (`owned`, `cc0`, `cc-by`, `cc-by-sa`, `licensed`, `unknown`);
- attribution and source URL, when applicable;
- tags that help the editor find it.

If the license is unknown, warn before publishing.

## User-provided assets

When the user says they will provide their own videos, do not ask for a path first. Create the project, run:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" open <slug>
```

This prints and opens `assets/source/` in the file manager. Tell the user to put the files there and say when they are done. If they prefer, they can pass a file path and you use `ingest --file`.

The user can:

- put files directly in `assets/source/`;
- pass a file path to `ingest --file`;
- put brand assets in a profile folder;
- replace a file and re-run `build`.

The agent should probe the file and update the manifest. If the user replaces a file with the same name, keep the old manifest entry or mark it stale; do not silently assume the old probe data is valid.

## Authorized links

Use `yt-dlp` only for content the user owns or has permission to use:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" ingest meu-video \
  --url "https://..." \
  --confirm-rights
```

Read `references/link-ingest.md` before downloading. Do not bypass DRM, paywalls, or access controls. Do not commit downloaded media to the skill repository.

## Library

`rooster/library/` holds reusable assets:

```text
library/
├── music/
├── sfx/
├── fonts/
├── overlays/
├── luts/
├── broll/
└── images/
```

A global library can live in `~/.rooster/library/`. Record the license and attribution for each reusable asset. Do not assume a file is licensed because it is in the library.

## Music bed

Music is part of the edit plan, not an afterthought. Add it to `edit/plan.json`:

```json
{
  "music": {
    "src": "assets/licensed/music/theme.mp3",
    "gainDb": -18,
    "license": "licensed",
    "attribution": "Track name - Artist"
  }
}
```

Before declaring no music, look in `assets/source/`, `assets/licensed/music/`, `library/music/`, and any folder the user mentions. If you find candidates, ask which one to use. Do not assume the library is empty.

Use `library/music/` or a user-provided track. The build trims/loops it to the video duration and mixes it under the voice. For a still-image base, add the track in the engine instead. If there is no music, state that in `notes` instead of leaving the plan silent.

## Generated media

Generation is pluggable. The skill can call:

- HyperFrames `tts` (local Kokoro) or `/media-use` for voice/music;
- an approved TTS provider (ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Gemini, Edge TTS);
- an image/video generation provider if the user configures one.

Generation requires explicit permission and, usually, an API key. Never generate a real person's voice or likeness without consent. Never send private media to a provider without permission.

## Internet search and stock

Current v1 does **not** search stock libraries or the open web automatically. The agent can:

- download a URL the user provides;
- suggest search terms and let the user choose;
- record the source and license.

A future adapter can add Pexels/Unsplash/Pixabay search, but it must keep the license metadata and attribution.

## Adjusting assets

Change the channel default:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel set en-tech assets.strategy user
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel set en-tech assets.allowDownload false
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel set en-tech assets.allowGenerate true
```

Or change the workspace fallback:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" config set assets.strategy user
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" config set assets.allowDownload false
```

Or override per project in `project.json`:

```json
{
  "assets": {
    "strategy": "user",
    "sources": ["user"],
    "licensePolicy": "strict"
  }
}
```

After changing the strategy, tell the user what is now allowed and what is not. Re-run `build` only if the asset set or plan changed.

## Decision guide

- **User has footage** → `user` or `mixed`.
- **User has a YouTube reference** → `link`, after confirming rights.
- **Faceless explainer with no files** → `generated` or `none`; ask before generating.
- **Brand video** → `user` + a profile with logo/fonts.
- **No assets at all** → `none`; use motion graphics, type, and original audio/TTS if allowed.
- **Stock footage** → `library` or `licensed`; record license and attribution.

## Guardrails

- Do not download without permission.
- Do not generate a person's voice/likeness without consent.
- Do not use unlicensed music, fonts, or footage.
- Do not hide missing assets behind placeholders.
- Do not commit media, cookies, or API keys to the repo.

# Edit plan The edit plan is the bridge between the transcript analysis and the build. It is the artifact the user approves before any engine project is created. It lives at `channels//projects//edit/plan.json`. ## Schema ```json { "schema": "rooster.plan/v1", "source": "assets/source/video.mp4", "style": "style.md", "language": "pt-BR", "duration": 612.4, "summary": "Interview about starting a business after losing a job.", "music": { "src": "assets/licensed/music/theme.mp3", "gainDb": -18, "license": "licensed", "attribution": "Track name - Artist" }, "cuts": [ { "id": "cut-001", "start": 12.4, "end": 18.2, "reason": "long-pause", "confidence": 0.9 }, { "id": "cut-002", "start": 41.0, "end": 46.5, "reason": "retake", "note": "The next take is stronger", "confidence": 0.95 } ], "keeps": [ { "id": "keep-001", "start": 18.2, "end": 41.0, "reason": "strongest explanation of the problem" } ], "elements": [ { "id": "el-001", "type": "letreiro", "start": 3.0, "end": 6.0, "text": "A virada", "description": "Title card with the video's core promise", "style": "bold uppercase, accent color" }, { "id": "el-002", "type": "grafico", "start": 32.0, "end": 38.0, "text": "3 decisões", "description": "Three-step diagram appears one item at a time" }, { "id": "el-003", "type": "zoom", "start": 52.0, "end": 55.0, "description": "Slow punch-in on the speaker's face at the key insight" }, { "id": "el-004", "type": "broll", "start": 58.0, "end": 64.0, "src": "assets/source/broll-office.mp4", "description": "Office b-roll over the line about the first client" } ], "chapters": [ { "start": 0, "title": "Introdução" }, { "start": 45, "title": "O problema" } ], "notes": [ "Keep the original audio; no music under the first 5 seconds." ] } ``` ## Edit mode Set `editMode` at the top of the plan: | Value | Use | Model | |---|---|---| | `cleanup` (default) | Keep the full story; remove silence, filler, false starts, and abandoned retakes. | `cuts` | | `condensed` | Highlight or short version; select the best spans. Requires explicit user approval. | `keeps` | | `manual` | The user supplied an EDL; do not add cuts. | either | Do not mix `cuts` and `keeps` in one plan. `plan --check` rejects `keeps` without `editMode: "condensed"` and warns when cleanup removes more than 25% of the source. ## Cut reasons Use consistent values so the plan can be reviewed and automated: | Reason | Meaning | |---|---| | `long-pause` | Silence longer than the threshold | | `repetition` | The same idea is said again | | `false-start` | The speaker restarts the sentence | | `retake` | A later take is better | | `filler` | "um", "é", "tipo", "you know" | | `mistake` | Factual error or slip | | `off-topic` | Does not serve the story | | `manual` | User requested a cut | A cut is a removal from the source. Cleanup uses `cuts`. A condensed edit uses `keeps`. Do not mix the two models in the same plan; pick one and state it in `editMode`. ## Element types | Type | Use | |---|---| | `letreiro` | Title, key phrase, chapter card | | `grafico` | Chart, diagram, comparison, number | | `lista` | Steps, checklist, ranking | | `zoom` | Punch-in, emphasis, reaction | | `broll` | Footage or image over the voice | | `lower-third` | Name, role, location | | `caption-emphasis` | Highlight a word or phrase | | `transition` | Wipe, slide, fade between ideas | | `end-card` | CTA, subscribe, next video | | `custom` | Agent-authored HTML/CSS/GSAP or a reusable component | Each element needs `start`, `end`, and `description`. `text` is optional but encouraged for anything with words. ## Time base `cuts` and `keeps` are **source** times. `elements` and `chapters` are **source** times too, because the build remaps them through the cuts. The `plan` command writes both values to `plan.md` and `plan.html`: the raw time and the final time after the cuts. Approve the final time; the raw time is only for finding the moment in the source. ## Structured templates Do not rely on the generic card fallback. Pick a template and give it the data it needs. The renderer draws real motion for these; `description` is a production note and is never placed on screen. | `template` | Use | `data` | |---|---|---| | `chapter` | Section card | `{ kicker, sub }` | | `title` | Opening or key promise | `{ sub }` | | `diagram` | Process, flow, comparison | `{ nodes: string[], caption, kicker }` | | `counter` | Numbers, before/after, time saved | `{ rows: [{ value, label }], kicker }` | | `list` | Steps, features, recap | `{ items: string[], title }` | | `lower-third` | Name and role | `{ name, role }` | | `emphasis` | Highlight or correction | `{ text, strike, tag }` | | `callout` | Short corner label | `{ label, sub, icon }` | | `terminal` | Command, file, technical detail | `{ command, note }` | | `end-card` | CTA | `{ title, sub }` | | `custom` | Agent-authored HTML/CSS/GSAP | inline `html`, `css`, `animation`, or a `component` | Use `role: "chapter"` on a `letreiro` when it is a section card. Chapter cards are exempt from transcript grounding. `position` is optional: `top-left`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-right`, `center`, `center-left`. The default keeps the face visible. `text` must be short, on-screen copy. Put the explanation in `description`, never in `text`. ## Custom components The agent can author a motion graphic that is not in the built-in vocabulary. Use `template: "custom"` and either inline fields or a reusable component. Inline, for a one-off: ```json { "id": "el-020", "type": "custom", "template": "custom", "start": 120.0, "end": 124.0, "html": "
novo
", "css": ".glow { position:absolute; inset:0; display:grid; place-items:center; } .ring { width:180px; height:180px; border:6px solid #8b5cf6; border-radius:50%; position:absolute; }", "animation": "tl.fromTo(root.querySelector('.ring'), { scale: 0.4, opacity: 0 }, { scale: 1, opacity: 1, duration: 0.7, ease: 'back.out(1.7)' }, start + 0.1);" } ``` Reusable, for the channel's visual language: ```json { "id": "el-021", "type": "custom", "template": "custom", "component": "chapter-glow", "start": 240.0, "end": 244.0 } ``` The build looks for `chapter-glow` in this order: 1. `/style/components/chapter-glow/` 2. `/channels//style/components/chapter-glow/` 3. `/channels//profiles//components/chapter-glow/` 4. `/profiles//components/chapter-glow/` 5. `~/.rooster/profiles//components/chapter-glow/` 6. `/templates/profiles//components/chapter-glow/` 7. `/templates/components/chapter-glow/` A component folder contains: - `element.html` (or `index.html`) — the markup. - `element.css` (or `style.css`) — optional CSS, injected once. - `element.js` (or `animation.js` / `index.js`) — optional GSAP statements. The animation runs inside the composition timeline with these variables: - `root` — the wrapper element (`#el-`). - `start` — the element start in the final timeline, in seconds. - `duration` — the element duration, in seconds. - `tl` — the paused GSAP timeline that HyperFrames seeks. Use `tl.fromTo(root.querySelector(...), ...)` and `start + 0.1`. Do not create a separate timeline; HyperFrames will not seek it. Put scripts in `element.js`/`animation`, not inline in `element.html`. Custom elements are trusted local HTML/CSS/JS. They are supported by HyperFrames (including the FilmCraft element path), not by Remotion. FilmCraft + Remotion fails with a clear message. Custom components should use inline SVG/CSS; for media, use a `broll` element so the asset pipeline and license tracking still apply. The first time the agent invents a look that works, save it as a component. The next video can reuse it, and the channel's visual language accumulates instead of starting from zero. ## B-roll layout `broll` accepts `layout`: - `pip` — the b-roll sits in a large rounded card in the top-right; the speaker stays visible. This is the default and the right choice for talking-head footage. - `split` — the b-roll takes the top 58% and leaves the lower part of the frame visible. Use it when the screen recording needs more width. - `full` — only when the b-roll is the subject and the face does not need to stay on screen. Every b-roll needs: - `covers` — the exact line it is illustrating; - `intent` — `evidence` (the actual UI or action is the proof), `texture` (visual variation), or `transition` (covers a cut); - `sourceTime` — where in the raw the clip was extracted, in source seconds. `plan --check` compares `sourceTime` with the placement. If the clip comes from a later scene (more than 30 s ahead) and it is not marked `evidence`, it warns: use a custom motion graphic or a same-context clip. Even an `evidence` clip gets a spoiler warning; the editor must confirm it does not reveal a demo that happens later. B-roll is not a substitute for a designed beat. If the line is conceptual (an idea, a comparison, a promise), prefer a `diagram`, `counter`, `emphasis`, or `custom` element. Use b-roll when the real footage is the evidence. ## Visual rhythm A cut-only plan is not a finished video. Before showing the plan, check: - at least one visual beat every 20–40 seconds; - no stretch longer than 45 seconds without a letreiro, graphic, list, b-roll, lower-third, or end card; - alternate templates: a diagram, a counter, a list, a b-roll, an emphasis, a callout; - a chapter card does not replace the need for beats inside the chapter; - every long silence jump (6 s or more) has a PIP/split b-roll, a transition, or a deliberate punch-in; - captions and graphics quote or paraphrase the line that is being spoken, and use `covers` when the connection is not obvious. `plan --check` reports density gaps, unsupported element types, orphan cuts, ungrounded text, and b-roll without `covers`. `qa/plan-review.md` lists all of them. Fix the top warnings before building; use `build --strict-plan` when the plan should be clean. ## Cut smoothing The build softens the cut pass automatically: - a 35 ms audio micro-fade at every join (no clicks, no hard consonant cut); - a small punch-in on uncovered silence cuts, alternating wide/tight so the eye reads two camera angles; - `--cut-punch ` changes the punch (default `1.035`; `1` disables it); - `--cut-fade ` changes the audio fade (default `0.035`; `0` disables it). Covered cuts (a b-roll or transition overlaps the join) are not punched. `plan --check` lists the long jumps that still have no visual cover, the orphan reactions, and keeps shorter than 0.8 seconds that will read as a flash. ## Advanced fields | Field | Use | Reference | |---|---|---| | `music` | Music bed, ducking, gain, license | `features/audio.md` | | `sfx` | Sound effects at timeline positions | `features/audio.md` | | `color` | LUT, EQ, temperature, denoise, stabilize | `features/color.md` | | `multicam` | Camera list and camera cuts | `features/multicam.md` | | `zoom` / `transition` | Scale moves and overlay transitions | `features/motion.md` | | `chart` on `grafico`/`lista` | Bar, line, or pie data visualization | `features/charts.md` | ## Creative minimum A cut-only plan is incomplete unless the user explicitly asked for a clean cut. Before showing the plan, check: - at least one visual element (letreiro, lower-third, graphic, list, zoom, b-roll, or end card); - no stretch longer than 45 seconds without a beat (see **Visual rhythm** above); - music, or a `notes` entry explaining why there is none; - captions or on-screen text for key lines, or a `notes` entry explaining why there are none. If one of these is missing, add it or ask the user. Do not present "no overlays, no music, no captions" as a finished creative draft. Captions are not generated automatically by `build` in this version. If the video needs full captions, add a caption pass or `caption-emphasis` elements; do not claim captions in the delivery unless they are present in the draft. `music` is optional but explicit: ```json { "music": { "src": "assets/licensed/music/theme.mp3", "start": 0, "end": 60, "gainDb": -18, "license": "licensed", "attribution": "Track name - Artist" } } ``` `src` is relative to the project. `gainDb` defaults to `-18`. The build mixes the track under the voice and fades it in/out. ## Heuristics ### Cuts Cleanup is the default. Do not turn a long recording into a highlight unless the user explicitly asked for a shorter version and the plan says `editMode: "condensed"`. - Remove pauses longer than 0.7–1.0 s, unless the pause is dramatic. - Remove repeated takes; keep the last or strongest one. - Remove false starts and self-corrections when they do not add personality. - Remove filler words, but do not make the speaker sound unnatural. - Keep breaths and reactions that carry emotion. - Do not cut every pause; rhythm needs air. ### Silence cleanup Use the transcript as the baseline for cleanup: ```bash node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" silence --json node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" silence --min 0.8 --pad 0.08 ``` The command proposes `cuts` with `reason: "long-pause"` for every gap between transcript segments above `--min`, plus leading and trailing dead air. It is a dry run by default. Review the list, remove false positives (music-only beats, dramatic pauses, room tone that belongs in the edit), then write it: ```bash node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" silence --write ``` `--write` merges the new cuts into `edit/plan.json`, sets `editMode: "cleanup"`, and leaves existing non-silence cuts alone. If the plan already uses `keeps`, it refuses unless you pass `--force`; `--replace` discards the existing cuts before writing. Do not invent silence cuts by hand when the transcript can produce them. ### Elements - Add a letreiro when the speaker introduces a new chapter or a key phrase. - Add a graphic when the speaker cites a number, a comparison, or a process. - Add a list when the speaker enumerates steps or items. - Add a zoom when the speaker lands an insight or a punchline. - Add b-roll when the speaker describes a concrete noun or action. - Do not add an element to every sentence; the video becomes noise. - Do not use a full-screen panel or card to hide a mismatched slide unless the user explicitly asks. Prefer small lower-thirds, corner labels, captions, and overlays. The video must remain visible. - Match the element style to `style.md` and the resolved profile. ### Music - Prefer `library/music/` or a track the user provided with a known license. - If the user says the music is in a folder, search that folder and the project asset folders before declaring no music. - Use `gainDb` around `-18` under voice; `-6` to `-12` for music-only. - Use `start`/`end` to trim the track. The build loops and pads it to the video duration. - If there is no track, add `notes: ["no music requested"]` and do not claim music in the delivery. - Never use unlicensed music. ### Chapters - Use the analysis to find natural topic changes. - A chapter should start on a sentence boundary and make sense on its own. - Keep chapters at least 20–30 seconds apart for long videos. ## Showing the plan Before building, show a readable summary: ```md # Plano de edição Fonte: assets/source/video.mp4 (10:12) Estilo: style.md ## Cortes (12) - 00:12–00:18 — pausa longa - 00:41–00:46 — take repetido; o próximo é melhor ... ## Elementos (8) - 00:03–00:06 — letreiro: "A virada" - 00:32–00:38 — gráfico: "3 decisões" - 00:52–00:55 — zoom no rosto ... ## Capítulos - 00:00 Introdução - 00:45 O problema ... Aprovar este plano? Só vou criar a timeline e os visuais depois do seu OK. ``` `node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" plan ` writes the same summary to `edit/plan.md`, `edit/plan.html`, and `qa/plan-review.md`. If the harness can display a file or open a browser, show `edit/plan.html` in the review pane or browser. Otherwise, paste the summary in chat and give the file path. Ask for approval with the progress marker, for example: `Etapa 4/8 - Plano pronto. Posso seguir com a timeline?` The HTML review includes a player, clickable timecodes, the transcript context for each cut and element, and a **Textos para revisar** table. The context is there so the user can approve a cut without opening the raw transcript. Wait for an explicit approval. If the user changes the plan, update `edit/plan.json` and show it again. Run `textcheck ` before the final approval to list every on-screen text. ## Validation `node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" plan --check` should verify: - `schema` is `rooster.plan/v1`; - `source` exists; - `style` exists; - every cut has `start < end` and a `reason`; - every element has `start < end`, `type`, and `description`; - no element extends past the source duration; - if `music` exists, `music.src` exists; - the plan has at least one visual element unless `notes` records a clean-cut request; - the plan has a music decision, or `notes` records that no music was requested; - no duplicate ids; - chapters are sorted by start time; - when `edit/transcript.json` has word-level timestamps, no cut starts or ends inside a word (warning). The human-readable summary comes from `plan `; `--check` validates without printing the full summary. ## Mapping to the build - Cuts -> applied by `build` with FFmpeg; element timings are remapped to the cut timeline. - Elements -> generated as HyperFrames elements or Remotion components. - Chapters -> markers and optional YouTube chapters. - Style -> profile tokens or `style.md`. - Approval -> the gate before `build`. Run `build` only after the plan is approved: ```bash node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" build meu-video --engine hyperframes node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" build meu-video --engine remotion ``` `build` refuses a cut-only plan or a plan with no music decision unless `notes` records the exception or you pass `--allow-cut-only` / `--allow-no-music` after the user explicitly asks for it. Do not skip the plan. A bad plan costs minutes to fix; a bad render costs hours.

# Engines RoosterEdit is engine-agnostic. This document explains how to choose and drive each engine, and what the adapter contract looks like. The two creative engines are **HyperFrames** and **Remotion**. FFmpeg is the media utility: it probes, cuts, burns captions, mixes audio, and assembles. It is not a third creative engine. **FilmCraft** is an optional timeline target, not a creative engine. It receives the base cut and audio mix from FFmpeg and transparent element clips from HyperFrames or Remotion, then assembles an editable project. It is never the default and is never required. ## Decision tree ```text Did the user explicitly choose an engine? ├─ Yes → use it, unless it cannot do the job; explain the tradeoff. └─ No ├─ Does the user want an editable timeline to finish by hand (FilmCraft)? │ ├─ Yes → --target filmcraft; HyperFrames or Remotion renders the element clips │ └─ No │ ├─ No Node or no FFmpeg? │ │ └─ Produce the plan; explain that HyperFrames/Remotion need Node, and FFmpeg covers cuts/audio. │ ├─ Is the core job cutting real footage? │ │ ├─ Simple cuts, captions, audio → FFmpeg │ │ └─ Complex overlays, data, React components → Remotion │ ├─ Is it 3D? │ │ ├─ React project or needs @remotion/three → Remotion │ │ └─ HTML project or needs Three.js inside a web composition → HyperFrames │ ├─ Is it HTML/CSS/GSAP, kinetic type, charts, maps, motion graphics? │ │ └─ HyperFrames │ └─ Is it React, data-driven, or component-heavy? │ └─ Remotion ``` The default is `auto`. Respect the user's preference when they have one. ## Ask before building `auto` is a safe default, not a silent decision. Before the first build, ask once per project: > "Como você quer montar este vídeo? HyperFrames é o padrão e já está pronto. Remotion é melhor para React/3D, mas não está instalado. FilmCraft abre a timeline para edição manual, mas o MCP ainda não está configurado. Qual prefere?" - Match the question to `doctor --json` and `filmcraft status --json`. Do not claim something is missing when it is installed. - Skip the question when the user already chose an engine or explicitly asked for `auto`. - **Remotion:** after the scaffold, it needs `npm install` inside `engine/remotion`. Ask before installing; never install silently. If the user declines, fall back to HyperFrames and say so. - **FilmCraft:** it needs the CLI and the MCP. Ask before writing MCP config; the user must restart the agent for the tools to appear. FilmCraft is a timeline target, not an engine: still choose HyperFrames or Remotion for the element clips. - Record the decision in `project.json` (`engine`, `timeline`) and in `review.md`. ## Build from plan Once the plan is approved, generate the engine project: ```bash node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" build meu-video --engine hyperframes node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" build meu-video --engine remotion ``` The build: - validates `edit/plan.json`; - applies the plan's cuts with FFmpeg, or reuses a cached base when the source, keeps, format, and mix are unchanged; - remaps element and chapter timings to the cut timeline; - copies the base media and element assets into the engine project; - writes a working composition for the chosen engine; - writes `work/build-state.json` and updates `project.json` with the engine and `preview` status. Use `--force` to rebuild an existing engine project, `--if-needed` to skip when the build state is unchanged, `--rebuild-media` to force FFmpeg again, and `--no-cache` to bypass the cache. `--sample 3` now builds a short montage around the selected elements instead of the whole timeline. Render through the CLI so the cache key, quality tier, workers, frame cache, and probe are consistent: ```bash node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" render meu-video --draft node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" render meu-video --final node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" render meu-video --draft --print ``` `--force` re-renders even when the key matches. HyperFrames accepts `--workers`, `--gpu`, `--resume`, and `--frames-cache-dir`; Remotion accepts `--concurrency`, `--gl`, and `--frames`. ## FilmCraft (optional timeline target) FilmCraft is opt-in with `--target filmcraft` on `build` or `new`; the default target stays `auto`. The full set is `--target auto|hyperframes|remotion|filmcraft`. The build is hybrid: 1. FFmpeg builds the base cut and audio mix, as it does for the other engines. 2. HyperFrames or Remotion renders each visual element as its own transparent clip: - HyperFrames: MOV ProRes 4444 with alpha, one composition per element. - Remotion: ProRes 4444 with PNG frames and `yuva444p10le`, one composition per element. Remotion needs a one-time `npm install` in `engine/filmcraft/remotion`; ask before installing. The build reports that path when the CLI is missing. 3. FilmCraft assembles an editable `.fcproj`: source on V1 (video only), the mixed audio on A1, element clips on V2+ (greedy non-overlapping lanes), markers for chapters/elements/cuts, and captions when an SRT or VTT exists. ```bash node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" build meu-video --target filmcraft --engine hyperframes node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" build meu-video --target filmcraft --engine remotion node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" build meu-video --target filmcraft --if-needed node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" timeline meu-video --open node "/scripts/rooster.mjs" render meu-video --draft ``` `--engine hyperframes|remotion` selects the element renderer; `auto` picks Remotion for 3D elements and HyperFrames otherwise. The CLI is used for deterministic builds; the MCP server is for interactive editing and is not required for `build`. The project records `timeline: "filmcraft"` and `engine` as the element renderer. FilmCraft cannot animate the base clip or apply overlay transitions. A plan with `zoom` or `transition` fails the FilmCraft build instead of silently dropping the motion; use `--target hyperframes`/`remotion`, replace those layers with punch-ins and PIP/split b-roll, or pass `--allow-skipped-elements` if the omission is deliberate. FilmCraft is MIT OR Apache-2.0 and still alpha; Windows is less tested. Read `references/nle-handoff.md` for the project layout, incremental builds, render, and caveats; read `references/timeline.md` for the adapter mapping. ## HyperFrames HyperFrames renders HTML/CSS/media to deterministic MP4 by seeking a paused timeline frame by frame. It is a strong fit for motion graphics, kinetic typography, charts, maps, overlays, captions, and HTML-based 3D. ### When to use - faceless explainers and social shorts; - kinetic type and text-heavy scenes; - data visualization, charts, maps; - HTML overlays on footage; - 3D scenes inside an HTML composition; - projects where the user wants the HyperFrames Studio editing surface. ### Commands ```bash npx hyperframes init npx hyperframes preview npx hyperframes check --json npx hyperframes snapshot --review npx hyperframes timeline --json npx hyperframes render --quality draft -o draft.mp4 npx hyperframes render --quality delivery -o final.mp4 ``` If the `hyperframes` skill is installed, load it and follow its contract. If not, use the commands above and the render contract below.
