# Token discipline

Video work is naturally expensive: transcripts, frames, plans, render logs, and generated code. The goal is not to reduce quality; it is to keep noisy data out of the model context and reserve tokens for creative decisions.

## Rule 0 — Delegate the raw material

The cheapest token is one the main agent never reads. Send the stages that produce or consume raw material to a stage subagent: transcript analysis, research, script and plan drafts, style, build, QA, render. The subagent reads the file, writes the artifact, and returns a handoff of 15–25 lines. The main agent keeps the brief, the decisions, the gates, and the final visual judgment.

This is not only about speed. A transcript read in stage 3 is still occupying context in stage 8, and every later turn pays for it again. The handoff is paid once. The full protocol and the role files are in `references/subagents.md` and `agents/`.

If the harness has no fresh-context agent tool, or a spawn fails, keep the same file boundaries: write the raw output to `work/logs/` or `work/scratch/`, read only the summary, and do the stage inline.

## Rule 1 — Never paste long logs

HyperFrames, Remotion, FFmpeg, and Whisper can print thousands of lines. Redirect them to a log file and read only the tail or the JSON summary.

```bash
# HyperFrames render
npx hyperframes render --quiet -o ../../renders/draft.mp4 > render.log 2>&1
tail -n 20 render.log
```

```powershell
# Windows
npx hyperframes render --quiet -o ../../renders/draft.mp4 *> render.log
Get-Content render.log -Tail 20
```

```bash
# HyperFrames check
npx hyperframes check --json > check.json 2>&1
node -e "const d=require('./check.json'); console.log({ok:d.ok, errors:d.lint?.errorCount, warnings:d.lint?.warningCount})"
```

```bash
# Remotion
npx remotion render src/index.ts RoosterVideo out.mp4 --log=error
```

```bash
# FFmpeg
ffmpeg -v error -i input.mp4 ...
```

If a command fails, read the `Fix:` line, the JSON error, or the last 30 lines. Do not read the full log unless the summary is insufficient.

Keep these files in `work/logs/` (or `../../work/logs/` from inside the engine directory) so they stay out of the main context and out of the project's editorial folders.

## Rule 2 — Use the transcript digest, not the raw JSON

`transcript.json` contains segments and word-level timestamps. Word-level data is useful for captions but expensive to read. Use:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" digest meu-video --from 60 --to 180
```

This prints only the segments in the range. Use `--json` when you need structure. Read the full transcript only when the task truly needs every line.

For a long transcript:

1. Run `digest` with `--json`.
2. Use `transcript-analyst` (or a subagent with the same role file) to propose 10–20 candidate beats, cuts, and elements.
3. Review the compact result in the main context.

## Rule 3 - Use `plan`, not the raw plan

`edit/plan.json` can be large. The human-readable summary is enough for approval:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" plan meu-video
```

Read the JSON only when editing specific fields or debugging validation.

## Rule 4 — Read only the reference section you need

The `references/` directory is a library, not a checklist. Use the reference map in `SKILL.md` and read only the file for the current phase. Use `rg`/grep to find a section instead of loading a 300-line file.

Examples:

- engine choice: `references/engines.md`
- plan schema: `references/edit-plan.md`
- social/vertical: `references/intake.md`
- asset policy: `references/assets.md`

## Rule 5 — Inspect a few frames, not every frame

Use 3–5 representative frames per review:

- hook/first frame;
- a middle scene;
- a caption-heavy scene;
- a transition;
- the end card.

Use a contact sheet for broad coverage. Read individual frames only when the contact sheet raises a question.

## Rule 6 — Draft once, final once

- Render a low-quality draft for review.
- Fix the plan/style before re-rendering.
- Render the final only after approval.
- For text-only changes, use a still/snapshot instead of a full video render.

## Rule 7 — Reuse what is already done

- Do not re-transcribe the same file.
- Do not rebuild the engine project if only the plan text changed; update the plan and rebuild.
- Cache TTS per line and reuse unchanged audio.
- Reuse profiles, components, and templates.

## Rule 8 — Delegate by artifact, not by reflex

Subagents are the default for heavy stages, and the main thread should receive only the handoff:

- transcript analysis into `edit/analysis.json` and a compact beat list;
- research and reference gathering into `work/research.md`;
- script and plan drafts into the real project files;
- art direction and storyboard into `style.md` and `storyboard.json`;
- build, fixes, and QA into artifacts plus evidence paths;
- render and packaging into a path and probe stats.

Give the subagent file paths, not pasted content. Ask for the handoff template. Do not delegate the final creative decision, the approval gate, or the license call. Parallelize only independent work; serialize writes to the same plan, timeline, or engine project.

The full cast and contract are in `references/subagents.md`. Do not spawn a subagent for a one-line question; the fixed cost of a fresh context only pays off when the stage has real raw material.

## Rule 9 — Keep the main context clean

- Do not paste full `index.html`, `Video.tsx`, or generated code unless debugging.
- Use `rg` to find the relevant lines.
- Keep decisions in `review.md` and refer to the file path.
- Summarize the user's feedback in one sentence before acting.

## Rule 10 — Budget by phase

| Phase | Owner | Main thread reads |
|---|---|---|
| Onboarding | main | 1 short message, no file reads |
| Intake | main + `producer` | the brief summary, no full assets |
| Transcript | `transcript-analyst` | handoff only, never `transcript.json` |
| Plan | `editor` | view `plan.html` + handoff; JSON only for a field edit |
| Build | `engineer` | status + artifact paths; no code or logs |
| Preview | `qa` + main | 3–5 frames + handoff |
| QA | `qa` | verdict + evidence paths, not a full log |
| Delivery | `engineer` | final path + probe stats |

## Rule 11 — Close with a short report

- End in 5–10 lines: what is done, the paths, any blocker, and one next question.
- Do not repeat the brief, dump commands, or paste the full doctor table.
- Put details in the workspace or link the docs.
- After installation, the only next question is whether to configure the workspace now.

## What not to optimize

- Do not skip the plan approval to save tokens.
- Do not skip frame inspection to save tokens.
- Do not use a smaller model for the final editorial review.
- Do not compress the transcript so much that the story is lost.

Save tokens on **noise**, not on **judgment**.

# Video-inspired 6-step workflow

This fast path borrows the **sequence** and the **approval discipline** from the reference video "Como editar vídeos com IA usando o Claude Code" by Marcos Lemos. It does **not** copy the video's folder names. RoosterEdit keeps its own workspace structure and maps the video's concepts into it.


## Delegation

The steps map to the roles in `agents/`: `art-director` for Step 3, `transcript-analyst` for Step 4 transcription, `editor` for Step 4 plan, `engineer` for Steps 5–6 visual elements, build, and render, and `qa` for Step 6 review. The main agent keeps the plan approval gate and looks at the final frames.

Pass paths, not contents. The subagent writes the detail to the project and returns a handoff in `work/handoffs/`; logs go to `work/logs/`. Read `references/subagents.md` for the full protocol.

## Step 1 — Prepare the machine

Check and, if missing, install:

- FFmpeg
- Node.js LTS
- Python 3
- Whisper (local, free transcription)
- HyperFrames (via its skill or CLI)

Ask for permission before each installation. Test Whisper with a short audio file before relying on it.

```bash
ffmpeg -version
node --version
python --version
whisper --help
npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes
```

If the user only wants planning, do not install anything. Explain what is missing and continue with the plan.

## Step 2 — Create or resolve the project

Create the channel first if it does not exist, then the project:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" new meu-video \
  --channel meu-canal \
  --profile minimal \
  --source live \
  --voice user
```

Put raw media in `channels/meu-canal/projects/meu-video/assets/source/`. If the user says they will provide the footage and has not sent a path, create the project and run `open <slug>` so the source folder opens in the file manager. If the user already has a project, resolve its channel/profile instead of creating a new one.

## Step 3 — Write the style guide

Write `channels/<canal>/projects/<slug>/style.md` and resolve the profile. The video uses a single `ESTILO.md`; RoosterEdit separates the human-readable guide (`style.md`) from the reusable identity (`profiles/<id>/profile.json`).

The style guide should include:

- tone and references;
- palette and typography;
- motion and transitions;
- caption style;
- music and SFX palette;
- what to avoid;
- examples of frames or links.

## Step 4 — Transcribe and plan

### Transcribe

Prefer HyperFrames transcribe. It uses Parakeet for English and whisper.cpp for other languages, and writes word-level timestamps:

```bash
npx hyperframes transcribe channels/meu-canal/projects/meu-video/assets/source/video.mp4 \
  --language pt \
  --model small \
  --json \
  --to srt \
  -o channels/meu-canal/projects/meu-video/edit/captions/transcript.srt
```

Or use Whisper locally:

```bash
whisper channels/meu-canal/projects/meu-video/assets/source/video.mp4 \
  --model small \
  --language pt \
  --output_format json \
  --output_dir channels/meu-canal/projects/meu-video/edit
```

Save the result as `edit/transcript.json` (and optionally `.srt`). The transcript must include the start and end time of each sentence or segment.

The RoosterEdit CLI wraps both paths:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" transcribe meu-video --language pt --quality fast
```

It prefers Parakeet/sherpa-onnx when the language is covered, then faster-whisper, then whisper.cpp/OpenAI Whisper. `--quality fast` uses `base`, beam 1, and word timestamps only when captions are enabled; `balanced` uses `small` and `accurate` uses `medium`. Results are cached by source and options; rerunning without changes is instant.

### Plan

Work from `edit/analysis.json` and `style.md`, not from the raw transcript. Understand the subject and write `edit/plan.json`:

- cuts for long pauses, repetitions, false starts, and retakes;
- the strongest take to keep;
- overlays: letreiros, graphics, lists, zooms, b-roll;
- music: `src`, `gainDb`, and license, or a note explaining why there is none;
- start, end, and description for every cut and element;
- a short summary and chapter markers.

A cut-only plan is incomplete unless the user explicitly asked for a clean cut. Include at least one visual element and a music decision before showing the plan.

Read `references/edit-plan.md` for the schema and heuristics.

### Show the plan before building

Always show the user a readable summary of `edit/plan.json` and wait for approval. `plan <slug>` also writes `edit/plan.md`, `edit/plan.html`, and `qa/plan-review.md`; display the HTML artifact in the harness's preview pane or browser when available. Do not create the HyperFrames project, the timeline, or the final render before the plan is approved. This is the most important gate in the workflow.

## Step 5 — Create the visual elements

Turn the approved plan into scenes:

- **Letreiros**: short titles, names, key phrases.
- **Gráficos**: diagrams, charts, numbers, comparisons.
- **Listas**: steps, checklist items, rankings.
- **Zooms**: punch-ins on faces, products, or details.
- **B-roll**: footage or images that illustrate the words.
- **Lower thirds**: names and roles.

Choose the engine:

- HyperFrames for HTML/CSS/GSAP motion and automatic assembly;
- Remotion for React, data-driven scenes, and 3D;
- FFmpeg for simple cuts, captions, and audio.

Ask the user before building (see the gate in `references/engines.md`): HyperFrames is the default; Remotion needs `npm install` with permission; FilmCraft needs the MCP connected with permission and an agent restart. Do not choose silently when the engine is missing.

## Step 6 — Assemble, review, export

### Option 1 — Automatic assembly

Build a HyperFrames project from the approved plan:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" build meu-video --engine hyperframes
```

The build applies the plan's cuts with FFmpeg, remaps the element timings, copies the media, and writes a working composition. Base media and mixes are cached; `--if-needed` skips unchanged builds, and `--sample 3` builds a short montage for approval. Preview it in the browser. Review the cuts, captions, overlays, and audio. Render to `renders/final.mp4`.

### Option 2 — Remotion

Build a Remotion project from the approved plan when the video needs React components, data-driven scenes, interaction, or 3D via `@remotion/three`:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" build meu-video --engine remotion
```

After the scaffold, ask before running `npm install` in `engine/remotion`; if the user declines, fall back to HyperFrames. Preview in Remotion Studio, then render to `renders/final.mp4`.

### Review and export

Run the QA sweep through `qa` and the fixes through `engineer`:

- Watch the draft with the user.
- Fix timing, captions, audio, and visual issues.
- Render the final.
- Validate with FFprobe.
- Deliver `renders/final.mp4`, `edit/captions/captions.srt`, `renders/thumbnail.png`, and `renders/metadata.json`.

## What we keep from the video

- The 6-step sequence.
- The idea of a single visual style guide.
- Local Whisper transcription with timestamps.
- An edit plan with cuts and visual elements.
- A hard approval gate before building.
- Two assembly paths: HyperFrames for HTML/GSAP motion, Remotion for React/3D/data.
- A final review and export step.

## What we adapt

- Folder names: we use `channels/<canal>/projects/<slug>/` instead of `bruto/estilo/trabalho/final`.
- The style guide is split into `style.md` and a reusable profile.
- The plan is `edit/plan.json`, not `trabalho/plano.json`.
- The plan feeds an engine-agnostic timeline (`edit/timeline.json`), not only one engine.
- Channels and profiles make the workflow reusable across videos.
- QA, licenses, captions, and delivery are first-class.

## Anti-patterns

- Copying the video's folder names literally when the project already has a structure.
- Building before the plan is approved.
- Skipping the style guide and improvising the look.
- Treating automatic captions as final.
- Creating overlays for every sentence instead of for the moments that need them.
- Rendering before watching the preview.
- Trying to force HyperFrames into a React/3D project instead of using Remotion.

# Workflow

This is the full RoosterEdit pipeline. Read it once at the start of a project, then return to the relevant phase when needed. The phases are ordered, but real projects loop: a QA finding can send you back to the storyboard, and a missing asset can change the script.

## Phase 0 — Discover

1. Find the workspace (`rooster/` or `ROOSTER_WORKSPACE`). If none exists, ask before creating one.
2. Run `node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" doctor --json`.
3. Read `references/harness.md` if a capability is missing.
4. Inspect any existing project files. Do not overwrite user work.
5. Ask only the intake questions that change the output (`references/intake.md`).

Exit criteria: you know what the user wants, what tools are available, and whether a workspace exists.

## Fast path (video-inspired)

For a single video with real footage, the shortest route is:

1. Prepare FFmpeg, Node, Python, Whisper, HyperFrames (with permission).
2. Create/resolve the project and put raw media in `assets/source/`.
3. `art-director` writes `style.md` and resolves the profile. Run `styleproof <slug>` and approve the three frames.
4. `transcript-analyst` transcribes to `edit/transcript.json` and writes `edit/analysis.json`; `editor` writes `edit/plan.json`; show the plan and wait for approval.
5. `engineer` builds the visual elements from the plan. Run `build --sample 3` and approve the sample first.
6. `engineer` assembles in HyperFrames or Remotion; `qa` reviews `preview/index.html` and the frames, then `engineer` renders to `renders/`. Use `export` for an NLE handoff.

Read `references/video-pipeline.md` for the full mapping. This is the default for single-video jobs; the rest of this document is the broader studio pipeline.

## Progress and gates

Keep a compact 8-step tracker and show the current step in every update: environment, intake, assets/transcript, plan, timeline, build, preview/QA, render/delivery. At each gate, name the next action and ask before continuing, for example `Etapa 4/8 — Plano pronto. Posso seguir com a timeline?` Do not print the whole checklist every time, and do not combine timeline and final render in one approval; preview and QA sit between them. The build gate includes the engine and timeline choice: HyperFrames (default), Remotion (install only with permission), or FilmCraft (connect the MCP only with permission). If a creative, audio, or cost decision is unclear, ask at the current step instead of guessing.

## Delegation

Every phase ends with a handoff. Run the heavy phases through the matching role in `agents/`: `producer` (brief), `researcher`, `transcript-analyst`, `scriptwriter`, `editor` (plan and timeline), `art-director`, `audio-director`, `engineer` (build, render, delivery), `qa`. The main agent keeps intake, the approval gates, and the final visual judgment.

Write summaries to `work/handoffs/` and raw command output to `work/logs/`. The main agent reads the handoff, a plan summary, and a few frames; it does not read the raw transcript, generated code, or full logs. Read `references/subagents.md` before the first spawn.

Parallelize only independent work. Research, script variants, and art-direction options can run together after the brief; writes to the plan, timeline, or the same engine project stay serialized.

## Phase 1 — Intake

Capture:

- goal and audience;
- platform and aspect ratio;
- declared duration, only when the user set a target; otherwise the edit defines it;
- edit mode (`cleanup` default; `condensed` only with explicit approval);
- source mode (`live`, `generated`, `hybrid`);
- voice mode (`user`, `tts`, `none`);
- style mode (`user`, `profile`, `ai`, `reference`);
- existing assets and links;
- autonomy (`auto`, `guided`, `manual`);
- hard constraints (deadline, brand rules, legal restrictions).

Do not ask twenty questions. Infer what you can from the brief and confirm the expensive-to-change decisions.

Exit criteria: a short, written intake summary the user can correct.

## Phase 2 — Research and references

Only when the video depends on facts, a visual reference, or a style the user cannot describe.

- Collect 3–5 visual references and note what specifically to borrow (palette, type, pacing, transitions).
- For factual content, verify claims and keep a source list.
- For a reference video, extract frames and describe the style in concrete terms, not adjectives.
- For a link source, read `references/link-ingest.md` and confirm rights before downloading.

Exit criteria: enough context to write a brief and a style direction without guessing.

## Phase 3 — Brief

Write `brief.md`:

```md
# <Project name>

## Goal
## Audience
## Platform and format
## Duration
## Tone
## Key message
## Call to action
## References
## Constraints
## Success criteria
```

A good brief is one page. If it is longer, the idea is not clear yet.

Exit criteria: the user agrees with the goal, format, and duration.

## Phase 4 — Script and beats

Write `script.md` and `script.json`.

The script should include:

- spoken lines (if voice is used);
- on-screen text;
- scene beats with approximate durations;
- visual notes for each beat;
- the hook and the CTA.

For a faceless explainer, the script is the spine. For a talking-head video, the transcript is the spine and the script is a paper edit; the plan still defaults to `cleanup` unless the user approved a `condensed` version. For a 3D short, the script may be a narration track plus a shot list.

Exit criteria: the user approves the story, or the `auto` mode logs the decision and moves on.

## Phase 5 — Style

Write `style.md` with:

- palette and contrast rules;
- typography and type scale;
- motion language and transitions;
- caption style;
- audio palette (music, SFX, voice);
- do/don't examples;
- AI style prompts, if images will be generated.

Resolve a profile if one exists. If not, create one from brand assets, from references, or from scratch. Keep the style specific enough to make decisions, but not so specific that every scene looks the same.

Exit criteria: the user can look at `style.md` and say "that's the video".

## Phase 6 — Assets

1. Ingest files into `assets/source`, `assets/generated`, or `assets/licensed`.
2. Download authorized links with `yt-dlp` into `assets/source/<slug>/`.
3. Probe every media file with FFprobe.
4. Build or update `assets/manifest.json`.
5. Generate proxies and thumbnails.
6. Flag missing assets, unknown licenses, and incompatible formats.

Do not build around an asset that might not exist. A placeholder is a bug.

Exit criteria: every scene has the assets it needs, or a documented fallback.

## Phase 7 — Storyboard

Write `storyboard/storyboard.json` and generate frames if possible.

Each scene should include:

- id, title, duration;
- visual description;
- camera/motion notes;
- on-screen text;
- voice line;
- audio/music cue;
- asset references;
- transition in/out;
- engine hints (2D, 3D, footage, overlay).

The storyboard is where pacing problems are cheapest to fix. A 20-scene storyboard that reads well is better than a beautiful render with a boring middle.

Exit criteria: the user approves the storyboard, or `auto` logs it.

## Phase 8 — Timeline and EDL

Translate the storyboard into `edit/timeline.json` and, for footage, `edit/edl.json`.

The timeline is the engine-agnostic source of truth for editorial decisions. It should include:

- format (width, height, fps, duration);
- tracks (video, overlay, captions, voice, music, SFX);
- clips with source in/out and timeline start/end;
- scenes with component/props references;
- markers for beats and QA;
- caption cues and audio cues.

Read `references/timeline.md` for the schema and adapters.

Exit criteria: the timeline adds up to the target duration, has no overlaps or gaps that are not intentional, and covers every scene.

## Phase 9 — Build

1. Choose the engine (`references/engines.md`).
2. Scaffold inside `channels/<channel>/projects/<slug>/engine/<engine>/`.
3. Implement scenes, components, captions, audio, and 3D.
4. Keep assets referenced from the project's `assets` directory.
5. Keep the code readable and editable.
6. Run the engine's lint/check command after structural changes.

For HyperFrames, follow its render contract: `class="clip"`, `data-start`, `data-duration`, deterministic timelines, no real-time clocks. For Remotion, use `useCurrentFrame()` and `Sequence`; avoid real-time side effects. For FFmpeg, generate a readable filter graph and keep the EDL as the source of truth.

Exit criteria: the project builds and renders at least one still or short draft.

## Phase 10 — Preview

Offer a preview before the final render:

- native studio (`npx hyperframes preview`, `npx remotion studio`);
- unified review page (`node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" preview <slug>`);
- draft render for FFmpeg projects.

Use a browser when available. Take screenshots at key beats, inspect console errors, and check the timeline. Without a browser, render stills and read them as images.

Exit criteria: the user has seen the video (or representative frames) and approved, or `auto` has performed the review and logged it.

## Phase 11 — QA

Run the checklist in `references/qa.md`.

At minimum:

- technical: resolution, aspect, fps, duration, black/freeze frames, audio loudness, clipping, silence, captions sync, safe areas;
- editorial: hook, clarity, pacing, CTA, brand consistency;
- legal: asset licenses, music, fonts, source rights;
- platform: aspect, duration, caption style, thumbnail, metadata.

Write `qa/report.md` with pass/fail and evidence. Fix cheap issues before the final render.

Exit criteria: no blocking issues.

## Phase 12 — Render and deliver

1. Render a draft.
2. Inspect the draft with FFprobe and by looking at frames.
3. Render the final.
4. Validate the final.
5. Package: MP4, captions, thumbnail, metadata, project archive.
6. Tell the user where everything is.

Do not upload or publish without explicit permission.

Exit criteria: a verified final file and a complete package.

## Phase 13 — Learn

- Save the profile or component if it is reusable.
- Record decisions and feedback in `review.md`.
- Promote a local profile to global if the user wants it.
- Update the channel defaults if a pattern should apply to future videos.

Exit criteria: the next project starts faster.

## Gates

| Gate | When | In `auto` |
|---|---|---|
| Brief | After intake | Log and proceed unless the goal is ambiguous |
| Script | After script/beats | Log and proceed unless facts or claims are risky |
| Style + storyboard | Before build | Log and proceed unless assets are missing |
| Rough cut / preview | Before final render | Review and proceed unless the user asked for approval |
| Final | Before delivery | Validate and deliver |

In `guided` mode, stop at every gate and wait. In `manual` mode, ask before changing any creative decision.

## Artifacts

| Artifact | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `project.json` | Project configuration and overrides |
| `brief.md` | Goal, audience, constraints |
| `script.md` / `script.json` | Spoken lines, text, beats |
| `style.md` | Visual and audio direction |
| `storyboard/storyboard.json` | Scene plan |
| `assets/manifest.json` | Asset inventory and provenance |
| `edit/timeline.json` | Engine-agnostic timeline |
| `edit/edl.json` | Footage cut list |
| `edit/captions/` | SRT/VTT and caption data |
| `engine/<engine>/` | Implementation |
| `preview/` | Review page and screenshots |
| `qa/report.md` | QA evidence |
| `renders/` | Draft, final, thumbnail |
| `review.md` | Decisions, feedback, lessons |

## Anti-patterns

- Building the engine before the script and storyboard are clear.
- Rendering before the user has seen a preview.
- Hardcoding colors, fonts, or durations that belong in a profile.
- Downloading a link without confirming rights.
- Treating automatic captions as final.
- Using a 4K source when 1080p is enough.
- Adding background music because "videos have music" instead of because the story needs it.
- Calling a render successful without probing the file and looking at frames.

# Bootstrap prompt (pt-BR)

Prompt para preparar o ambiente e começar um vídeo no fluxo inspirado no vídeo de referência, mas usando a estrutura do RoosterEdit. Cole no agente (OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code etc.) e ajuste os caminhos.

---

Quero editar meus vídeos com IA usando o RoosterEdit. Prepare este computador e este projeto:

1. Verifique e, se faltar, instale FFmpeg, Node.js LTS e Python 3. Peça minha permissão antes de cada instalação.
2. Instale o Whisper para transcrição local e gratuita e teste com um áudio curto.
3. Instale a skill HyperFrames:
   ```
   npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes
   ```
4. Crie a pasta e o primeiro canal:
   ```
   node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" init
   node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel new meu-canal --language pt-BR --format 16:9 --profile minimal
   node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel design meu-canal --from minimal --accent "#22d3ee" --motion calm
   node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" new meu-video --channel meu-canal
   node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" open meu-canal/meu-video
   ```
   Antes do `channel design`, me pergunte paleta, tipografia e motion/áudio. Não defina duração: o comprimento vem da edição.
   Abra a pasta `assets/source/` para eu colocar meu vídeo bruto.
5. Leia meu guia de estilo em `rooster/channels/meu-canal/projects/meu-video/style.md` (se eu não tiver um, crie a partir das minhas referências).
6. Use o subagent `transcript-analyst` para transcrever e montar o mapa editorial:
   ```
   node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" transcribe meu-canal/meu-video --model small --language pt
   ```
   Ele grava `edit/transcript.json`, `edit/digest.md` e `edit/analysis.json` e devolve só duração, tópicos, beats e flags. Não leia a transcrição inteira no contexto principal.
7. Use o subagent `editor` para criar `edit/plan.json` a partir de `edit/analysis.json`, `style.md` e do brief, com:
   - cortes para pausas longas, repetições, falsos começos e retomadas;
   - o melhor take a manter;
   - letreiros, gráficos, listas, zooms e b-roll, com início, fim e descrição.
8. **Sempre me mostre o plano antes de criar qualquer coisa.** Só crie a timeline, os visuais ou o render depois do meu OK.
9. Depois do OK, use o subagent `engineer` para gerar o projeto e montar a timeline:
   ```bash
   node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" build meu-canal/meu-video --engine hyperframes
   ```
   Se eu escolher React, dados ou 3D, use Remotion:
   ```bash
   node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" build meu-canal/meu-video --engine remotion
   ```
10. Use `qa` para a revisão e `engineer` para o render final. No fim, me dê um resumo curto (até 8 linhas) do que foi feito e do próximo passo. Não escreva um guia longo.

---

## Observações

- Os papéis dos subagents estão em `agents/`. O agente principal deve passar caminhos, não conteúdo, e ler só o handoff de `work/handoffs/`.
- Se o ambiente não tiver Node/FFmpeg, não finja o render: gere o plano e explique que HyperFrames/Remotion precisam de Node.
- Não baixe conteúdo de terceiros sem autorização.
- Use `style.md` como fonte de verdade do visual; se houver um profile, ele complementa.
- O plano é o gate mais importante: nada de build antes da aprovação.
- Sem suporte a subagents, faça as etapas inline, mas continue gravando os arquivos e lendo só resumos.

# Prompt de instalação e setup (pt-BR)

Copie o bloco abaixo e cole na conversa com o seu agente. Ele deve usar a pasta de skills que o seu harness já lê e pedir permissão antes de instalar qualquer coisa.

---

Instale e prepare o **RoosterEdit** neste projeto.

1. Antes de clonar, pergunte se quero instalação local no projeto (recomendada) ou global. Use a pasta de skills que este harness já lê; exemplos de local: `.opencode/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`; exemplos de global: `~/.config/opencode/skills`, `~/.claude/skills`. Não clone nada antes da minha resposta.
2. Clone https://github.com/WesleyQDev/RoosterEdit.git na pasta escolhida, com o nome `rooster-edit`.
3. Confirme que o `SKILL.md` está no lugar e rode o doctor da skill. Mostre só o essencial: o que está pronto e o que falta, em no máximo 6 linhas.
4. Se faltar Node.js, FFmpeg, FFprobe, Python 3 ou Whisper/faster-whisper, me peça permissão antes de instalar e explique o comando. Use winget no Windows, Homebrew no macOS ou o instalador adequado no Linux.
5. Se o HyperFrames não estiver disponível, pergunte se quero instalar agora. Não instale nada sem meu OK.
6. Não crie workspace, projeto ou vídeo ainda. Nesta etapa, só instale, valide o ambiente e deixe claro que eu não preciso rodar comandos: você executa e me mostra o resultado.
7. No fim, responda em no máximo 8 linhas: status da instalação, o que já está pronto, o que falta (se algo) e onde ler os detalhes. Não escreva um guia longo nem liste todos os comandos.
8. Termine com uma pergunta simples, sem jargão: **"Quer criar o primeiro canal agora? Pensa nele como a pasta daquele projeto: dentro dela ficam os vídeos, o estilo e os arquivos da marca ou cliente. Se sim, me diga o nome do canal e o que ele vai produzir?"** Se eu disser não, pare sem criar nada.
9. Se eu disser sim, use o nome que eu der (ou proponha um curto em kebab-case se eu não der), infira idioma, formato, voz e política de assets, mostre um resumo curto para eu ajustar e só então crie a pasta `rooster/` com `init` + `channel new`. Não faça as 12 perguntas de uma vez e não defina duração.
10. Depois do canal, crie a identidade: pergunte em um bloco só sobre paleta, tipografia e motion/áudio e rode `channel design <id>`. Se eu não tiver preferência, mantenha o perfil base e diga que dá para mudar depois.
11. Depois do setup, me diga em uma linha como começar o primeiro vídeo e ofereça o prompt de bootstrap.

Se o agente não souber onde ficam as skills, veja [`docs/INSTALL.md`](../docs/INSTALL.md) para os caminhos mais comuns. Custos esperados estão em [`docs/COSTS.md`](../docs/COSTS.md).

# Audio — music ducking and SFX

Use this layer when the edit needs a music bed, sound effects, or both. It turns the audio fields in `edit/plan.json` into an FFmpeg mix that keeps the voice intelligible and the delivery loudness on target.

SFX are part of the channel's audio identity, not an optional afterthought. Tech, ads, motion graphics, and high-energy styles usually want whooshes, clicks, impacts, and UI sounds. Documentary and minimal styles should use them sparingly. If the channel style is unclear, ask before planning the audio layer.

The helpers live in `scripts/features/audio.mjs`. They build filter graphs and argument arrays; they never spawn FFmpeg or touch the workspace.

## Plan fields

`plan.music` is optional. `src` is required when the object exists and is relative to the project root.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src` | string | — | Music file path. |
| `start` | number | `0` | Source in-point in seconds. |
| `end` | number | `start + duration` | Source out-point in seconds. |
| `gainDb` | number | `-18` | Music gain under the voice. |
| `duckUnderVoice` | boolean | `true` | Duck with `sidechaincompress`; `false` keeps constant gain. |
| `license`, `attribution` | string | — | Provenance metadata; not used by the mixer. |

`plan.sfx` is an optional array. `start` and `end` are **timeline** positions, not source in/out points. The source is trimmed from 0 to `end - start` and delayed to `start`.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | `sfx-<n>` | Stable id for review and QA. |
| `src` | string | — | SFX file path. |
| `start` | number | — | Timeline start in seconds. |
| `end` | number | — | Timeline end in seconds; must be greater than `start`. |
| `gainDb` | number | `-12` | SFX gain. Keep it below the voice. |

```json
{
  "music": {
    "src": "assets/licensed/music/theme.mp3",
    "start": 12,
    "end": 72,
    "gainDb": -18,
    "duckUnderVoice": true,
    "license": "licensed",
    "attribution": "Track name - Artist"
  },
  "sfx": [
    {
      "id": "whoosh-01",
      "src": "library/sfx/whoosh-02.wav",
      "start": 11.8,
      "end": 12.6,
      "gainDb": -12
    }
  ]
}
```

Music is looped with `-stream_loop -1` and capped at the video duration. A music `end` beyond the source file is a planning error: FFmpeg will pad the missing part with silence.

## How the mix is built

`buildDuckingFilter({ duration, musicStart, musicEnd, gainDb, duck })` returns a graph with voice on input 0 and music on input 1:

```text
[1:a]atrim=...,volume=0.1259,afade=...,apad=whole_dur=60[music];
[0:a]asplit=2[voice][sc];
[music][sc]sidechaincompress=threshold=0.05:ratio=8:attack=20:release=300[ducked];
[voice][ducked]amix=inputs=2:duration=first:normalize=0[aout]
```

- `duck: true` uses the voice as a sidechain key. The music drops under speech and releases after it.
- `duck: false` uses the constant-gain fallback: trim, fade, pad, then `amix` with no sidechain.
- The music fades in for 1.2 s and out for 1.5 s, shortened for very short cues.
- `amix` uses `normalize=0` so `gainDb` is the actual gain instead of being halved again.
- The final mix is normalized to -14 LUFS integrated with a -1.5 dBTP ceiling. Use `-16`/`-23` for podcast or broadcast targets if the project requires it.

`buildSfxFilters({ sfx, duration })` returns one fragment per usable clip, with input indices starting at 2 by default:

```text
[2:a]atrim=start=0:end=1.5,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS,volume=0.5012,adelay=2500:all=1[sfx0]
```

Pass `inputStart` when the SFX inputs do not begin after a music input. `normalizeMusic()` and `normalizeSfx()` are also exported for plans, previews, and validation code that need resolved timing and gain without building a filter.

## FFmpeg integration

`mixAudioArgs()` assembles the full argument list. `<skill>` below is the RoosterEdit base directory. The module does not resolve paths: convert `base.path` (usually under `engine/<engine>/assets/`), `music.src`, and each `sfx[].src` to absolute paths, or choose an FFmpeg `cwd` that resolves all of them.

```js
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { mixAudioArgs } from "<skill>/scripts/features/audio.mjs";

const args = mixAudioArgs({
  base: {
    path: "engine/hyperframes/assets/base.mp4",
    hasVideo: true,
    hasAudio: true,
    duration: 60,
    kind: "video",
  },
  music: {
    src: "assets/licensed/music/theme.mp3",
    start: 12,
    end: 72,
    gainDb: -18,
    duckUnderVoice: true,
  },
  sfx: [
    { id: "whoosh-01", src: "library/sfx/whoosh-02.wav", start: 11.8, end: 12.6, gainDb: -12 },
  ],
  out: "engine/hyperframes/assets/base-mixed.mp4",
  duration: 60,
});

const result = spawnSync("ffmpeg", args, {
  cwd: process.cwd(),
  encoding: "utf8",
  windowsHide: true,
});
if (result.status !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr);
```

Input order is base, music, then SFX. Video is stream-copied when the base has a video stream and the output is not audio-only. Audio is AAC 192 kbps for MP4/M4A/MOV, PCM for WAV, FLAC for FLAC, and MP3/Opus/Vorbis for those containers.

## Commands

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" audio <slug> [--input <path>] [--out <path>]
```

The command renders a preview of `plan.music` + `plan.sfx` into `assets/generated/audio-mix.mp4`. The plan remains the source of truth; `build` applies the same mix to the engine base.

## QA

- Voice remains intelligible at normal playback volume.
- Music is audible in gaps and clearly lower under speech.
- Ducking releases without pumping or a long recovery tail.
- SFX land on the intended frame and never mask a word.
- No clipping; true peak is at or below -1 dBTP.
- Integrated loudness matches the target (-14 LUFS for YouTube, -16 for podcasts, -23 for broadcast).
- The mix has no dropouts at music loop points or SFX boundaries.
- `ffprobe` confirms duration, sample rate, and channel layout.

## Limitations

- One music bed per plan; multiple simultaneous beds need separate passes.
- Ducking uses fixed threshold, ratio, attack, and release. There is no per-section volume automation or EQ-based de-esser.
- SFX always start at source time 0; there is no `in` field for one-shots.
- `mixAudioArgs` re-encodes the final audio and always applies `loudnorm` at a fixed -14 LUFS target; it is meant to be the final audio pass, not an intermediate stem. Change `LOUDNESS_FILTER` in the module for a different delivery target.
- Still-image projects are not automated; add the audio mix in the HyperFrames or Remotion project.
- The module does not probe media. Bad paths, unsupported codecs, or a music `end` past the file end fail in FFmpeg.
- Plan validation checks `sfx` ids, `src`, and timing; it does not yet validate every gain or all ducking parameters.
- `build` now uses `mixAudioArgs` for `plan.music` and `plan.sfx`; the `audio` command is a preview pass.

# B-roll

`scripts/features/broll.mjs` finds local video and image files, ranks them against the transcript, and proposes plan-compatible b-roll elements. It is a keyword helper, not a stock search.

> **Licensing:** this module only sees files on disk. It cannot detect or verify a license, attribution, or model release. The agent must confirm the rights for every suggested clip and record them in `assets/manifest.json` before publishing.

## Plan fields

A good b-roll element has more than a path:

```json
{
  "id": "el-014",
  "type": "broll",
  "layout": "pip",
  "start": 120.4,
  "end": 126.2,
  "src": "assets/source/broll/notes-editor.mp4",
  "covers": "importar aquela pasta do seu Obsidian ou do seu Notion",
  "intent": "evidence",
  "sourceTime": 1159.0,
  "description": "Editor de notas em PIP, mantendo o rosto visível"
}
```

- `layout`: `pip` (default; large rounded card in the top-right, face stays visible), `split` (b-roll on top, lower frame visible), or `full` (only when the b-roll is the subject).
- `covers`: the exact line the clip illustrates. `plan --check` warns when it is missing or not found around the element time.
- `intent`: `evidence`, `texture`, or `transition`.
- `sourceTime`: where in the raw the clip was extracted. If it is more than 30 s ahead of the placement and the intent is not `evidence`, the check suggests a custom motion graphic or a same-context clip.
- The clip must show the thing the line is talking about. A generic notes editor from a later cake demo is not a b-roll for "import your Obsidian folder"; it is a spoiler.

## Verification

Before approving a b-roll, extract a frame from the clip at its midpoint and look at it. Confirm:

- the image matches the spoken noun/action;
- it is not from a later scene or a different demo;
- the layout keeps the face and the UI text readable;
- the clip has no burned-in cursor movement that fights the current action.

`plan --check` can catch a missing `covers` and a text/transcript mismatch. It cannot see the image. The editor still has to watch it.

## Purpose

- Scan project and library folders for usable video/image files.
- Rank candidates by transcript keywords and explicit tags.
- Suggest `broll` elements with transcript-based timing.
- Keep the process local: no API keys, network calls, downloads, or external services.

## Inputs and outputs

### `listMediaFiles(dirs)`

Accepts one directory, an array of directories, or a media file path. Recursively collects video and image extensions, returns absolute paths sorted for deterministic output, and skips missing directories, permission errors, symlinks, and common non-media folders (`node_modules`, `.git`, `cache`, `.opencode`).

Video: `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.mkv`, `.webm`, `.avi`, `.m4v`, `.mts`, `.m2ts`. Image: `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`, `.gif`, `.bmp`, `.avif`, `.tif`, `.tiff`.

### `rankBroll({ files, transcriptText, tags })`

`files` accepts paths from `listMediaFiles` or objects such as manifest entries:

```js
{ path: "assets/source/office.mp4", tags: ["office", "client"], src: "assets/source/office.mp4" }
```

`transcriptText` accepts a string, a transcript object, or a segment array. `tags` accepts a string or array and is treated as extra target keywords, not as a filter.

Score weights:

| Match | Points |
|---|---|
| Requested tag in filename, folder, or file tags | +6 |
| Multi-word requested tag found as a phrase | +4 |
| Filename or file-tag keyword in the transcript | +3 |
| Folder keyword in the transcript | +1 |

Repeated words count once. Accents are folded and common English/Portuguese/Spanish stopwords are ignored. Returns all valid media files, highest score first:

```js
{
  path: "C:\\project\\assets\\source\\office.mp4",
  name: "office.mp4",
  type: "video",              // "video" | "image"
  score: 9,
  matches: ["client"],
  src: null,                  // preserved when the input object had src
  tags: []
}
```

A score of `0` means no keyword overlap, not bad footage.

### `suggestBrollElements({ files, transcript, max })`

Returns plan-compatible elements sorted by start time:

```js
{
  id: "el-004",
  type: "broll",
  start: 58,
  end: 64,
  src: "assets/source/broll-office.mp4",
  description: "B-roll office.mp4 over \"the first client meeting\" (matches: client)"
}
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `max` | `3` | Maximum suggestions |
| `baseDir` | `null` | Project root used to make absolute paths relative |
| `idPrefix` | `"el"` | Element id prefix |
| `startIndex` | `1` | First id suffix (`el-001`) |
| `minDuration` | `2` | Skip shorter transcript segments |
| `maxDuration` | `6` | Cap each suggestion's length |

Timing comes from transcript segments: the suggestion starts at the segment start and ends at the segment end or `maxDuration`, whichever is earlier. Files are matched against each segment's text. The function never reuses a file and never returns overlapping intervals. It returns an empty array when there are no segments, no valid files, or no keyword overlap.

## Plan fields

Merge the returned objects into `edit/plan.json`:

```json
{
  "elements": [
    {
      "id": "el-004",
      "type": "broll",
      "start": 58,
      "end": 64,
      "src": "assets/source/broll-office.mp4",
      "description": "B-roll office.mp4 over \"the first client meeting\" (matches: client)"
    }
  ]
}
```

`src` is relative to the project root. If you call the function without `baseDir`, absolute paths are returned; pass `baseDir` or supply an object with a relative `src` to keep the plan portable. For licensed footage, prefer `assets/licensed/` and add `license`, `attribution`, and `source` to `assets/manifest.json`.

## Commands

Run the CLI:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" broll <slug> [--dir <path>] [--tags office,client] [--max 3] [--limit 10] [--write]
```

It writes `edit/broll-suggestions.json`. `--write` appends the suggestions to `edit/plan.json`; review them with `plan --show` before building.

```js
import { listMediaFiles, rankBroll, suggestBrollElements } from "./scripts/features/broll.mjs";

const files = listMediaFiles(["assets/source", "assets/licensed", "library/broll"]);
const transcript = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("edit/transcript.json", "utf8"));

const ranked = rankBroll({
  files,
  transcriptText: transcript,
  tags: ["office", "client"],
});

const elements = suggestBrollElements({
  files,
  transcript,
  max: 3,
  baseDir: process.cwd(),
});

console.log(JSON.stringify({ top: ranked.slice(0, 5), elements }, null, 2));
```

Review the output, merge the elements into `edit/plan.json`, then validate and show the plan:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" plan <slug> --check
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" plan <slug> --show
```

Use `plan --show` as the approval gate. Do not build from suggestions you have not reviewed.

## Integration

- Run after transcription and before the plan is approved.
- Pass manifest objects with `tags` and `src` when available; filename-only matching is weaker.
- Renumber `id` values if the plan already uses them, and check overlaps with existing elements, music cues, and captions.
- Place approved files in `assets/source/` or `assets/licensed/`, record the license and attribution, and keep the plan `src` pointing at the final location.
- HyperFrames and Remotion already render `type: "broll"` elements as images or muted videos with object-fit cover, so approved elements can be built without a new element type.

## Limitations

- **Local suggestion only.** No stock search, network call, download, generation, or catalog UI. It only sees the directories passed to it.
- **No vision or semantics.** No ML scene detection, object recognition, embeddings, or synonym matching. "Car" does not match "automobile"; exact keyword and tag overlap drives the score.
- **File names matter.** A generic name such as `clip-001.mp4` has nothing to match. Add tags in manifest objects or rename files descriptively.
- **Licensing is out of scope.** The module cannot tell whether a file is owned, licensed, CC, or unknown. The agent must confirm rights and attribution before use.
- **No media probing.** Duration, resolution, fps, codec, and audio presence are not checked. Verify a short clip with `ffprobe`; otherwise the engine may freeze, loop, or crop it awkwardly.
- **Segment-level timing only.** It uses transcript boundaries, not shot changes, beats, or visual continuity. Suggestions may start or end mid-action.
- **No overlap awareness outside the call.** It prevents duplicates and overlaps among its own output, but does not read the existing plan or timeline. Merge carefully.
- **Heuristic confidence.** Scores are relative ranking aids, not probabilities or editorial judgment. Review every suggestion with eyes and ears before approval.
- **No writes.** The module returns data. It does not edit `edit/plan.json`; the agent owns the merge and the approval step.

# Captions

Turn a transcript into readable caption cues, SRT/VTT sidecars, and an optional FFmpeg burn-in. Captions are a separate layer: `build` does not burn them automatically in this version.

## Input and output

Input is `edit/transcript.json` in the `rooster.transcript/v1` schema:

```json
{
  "schema": "rooster.transcript/v1",
  "source": "assets/source/video.mp4",
  "language": "pt-BR",
  "duration": 612.4,
  "segments": [
    { "start": 12.4, "end": 18.2, "text": "This is what the speaker said." }
  ]
}
```

`writeCaptions({ transcriptPath, outDir })` writes:

- `captions.srt` — SubRip, UTF-8, LF, `HH:MM:SS,mmm`;
- `captions.vtt` — WebVTT, UTF-8, LF, `HH:MM:SS.mmm`;
- `captions.json` — derived cue data, `rooster.captions/v1`.

It does not modify the transcript. If `outDir` is omitted, it writes next to the transcript. A delivery pass can copy the files to `renders/`.

## Cue rules

Segments are cleaned, sorted, and clamped so cues never overlap. Long segments split at sentence and clause punctuation, then at word boundaries. Each cue holds at most two lines of about 42 characters. Timing is divided proportionally by visible characters inside the original segment; no time is invented outside it.

```js
import { buildCues, toSrt, toVtt, writeCaptions } from "./scripts/features/captions.mjs";

const cues = buildCues(transcript, { maxLineChars: 42, maxLines: 2 });
const srt = toSrt(cues);
const vtt = toVtt(cues);
const result = writeCaptions({
  transcriptPath: "rooster/channels/default/projects/demo/edit/transcript.json",
  outDir: "rooster/channels/default/projects/demo/edit/captions",
  maxLineChars: 42,
  maxLines: 2,
});
// result.files = { srt, vtt, json }
```

`captions.json`:

```json
{
  "schema": "rooster.captions/v1",
  "source": "assets/source/video.mp4",
  "language": "pt-BR",
  "transcript": "C:/.../edit/transcript.json",
  "generatedAt": "2026-11-03T00:00:00.000Z",
  "duration": 612.4,
  "options": { "maxLineChars": 42, "maxLines": 2 },
  "count": 180,
  "cues": [
    { "id": 1, "start": 0, "end": 2.4, "text": "First line.", "lines": ["First line."] }
  ]
}
```

## Burn-in

`burnArgs()` returns `{ args, command, filter }` and executes nothing. `burnCommand()` returns the printable string. The caller decides whether to run it.

```js
import { burnArgs } from "./scripts/features/captions.mjs";

const { args, command } = burnArgs({
  video: "renders/draft.mp4",
  srt: "edit/captions/captions.srt",
  out: "renders/final.mp4",
  style: { font: "Inter", size: 42, color: "#ffffff", stroke: "#000000", position: "bottom", marginV: 48 },
});
```

The filter quotes spaces and escapes Windows drive colons, brackets, commas, and semicolons. The args array is authoritative; the printable command is for review. Burn-in re-encodes video to H.264 and copies audio by default; use `crf`, `preset`, and `audio` to change that.

## Build integration

- Use `caption-emphasis` in `edit/plan.json` for a few on-screen key lines; use this module for full captions.
- Generate sidecars after `transcribe` and before final delivery.
- `build` does not burn captions automatically. Run `captions --burn` after the draft render, or add caption elements manually inside the engine.
- Do not claim captions in a delivery unless `captions.srt`, `captions.vtt`, or burned captions are actually present.

## Commands

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" captions <slug> [--out <dir>] [--max-chars 42] [--max-lines 2]
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" captions <slug> --burn renders/draft.mp4 [--out-video renders/captioned.mp4] [--dry-run]
```

The command writes the sidecars under `edit/captions/`. With `--burn`, it executes the FFmpeg burn and writes `renders/captioned.mp4` by default; `--dry-run` prints the command instead.

## QA

- Cues are in sync and never overlap.
- No cue exceeds two lines or roughly 42 characters per line.
- Reading speed is comfortable; split or shorten fast passages.
- Text stays inside the title-safe area when burned.
- SRT/VTT parse in a standard player and use UTF-8 without a BOM.
- Spelling, punctuation, and speaker changes are correct.
- Captions do not cover faces or key visuals.

## Limitations

- Cue splitting and timing are heuristic; review before delivery.
- No word-level karaoke, speaker diarization, translation, or automatic spellcheck.
- Punctuation determines clause breaks; unpunctuated transcripts fall back to word wrapping.
- A single word longer than the line limit cannot be split.
- Burn-in assumes an SRT file and H.264 output; complex or unusual paths should be previewed.
- Very short segments may receive millisecond-scale cues.

# Color — grading, LUT, denoise, stabilization

Use this layer when footage looks flat, mixed cameras do not match, or handheld shots need stabilization. It maps the optional `plan.color` object to FFmpeg video filters and a two-pass vidstab flow.

The helpers live in `scripts/features/color.mjs`. They build filters and argument arrays; they never spawn FFmpeg or touch the workspace.

## Plan fields

`plan.color` is optional. All fields are optional; identity values are omitted from the filter chain.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lut` | string | — | Path to a `.cube` or `.3dl` LUT. |
| `brightness` | number | `0` | `eq` brightness, -1..1. |
| `contrast` | number | `1` | `eq` contrast, 0..4. |
| `saturation` | number | `1` | `eq` saturation, 0..3. |
| `temperature` | number | `0` | -100 (cool) to 100 (warm). |
| `denoise` | boolean, number, string, object | `false` | `hqdn3d` or `nlmeans` settings. |
| `stabilize` | boolean | `false` | Run the two-pass vidstab flow. |

Denoise accepts `true`, a strength number, `"light"`, `"medium"`, `"strong"`, `"nlmeans"`, `"hqdn3d:<strength>"`, `"nlmeans:<strength>"`, or `{ "filter": "hqdn3d" | "nlmeans", "strength": ... }`.

```json
{
  "color": {
    "lut": "assets/licensed/luts/film.cube",
    "brightness": 0.02,
    "contrast": 1.08,
    "saturation": 1.12,
    "temperature": 12,
    "denoise": "light",
    "stabilize": true
  }
}
```

Keep the grade subtle. A LUT plus strong `eq` plus a temperature shift easily crushes skin tones or clips highlights. Review stills before rendering.

## Filter order

`buildColorFilters(color)` returns an array of strings in this order:

1. **Denoise** — `hqdn3d` or `nlmeans`. Do this before sharpening or grading.
2. **LUT** — `lut3d=file='...'`.
3. **EQ** — `eq=brightness=...:contrast=...:saturation=...`.
4. **Temperature** — `colorbalance` in shadows, midtones, and highlights.

```text
hqdn3d=2:1.5:3:2.25,
lut3d=file='assets/licensed/luts/film.cube',
eq=brightness=0.02:contrast=1.08:saturation=1.12,
colorbalance=rs=0.018:bs=-0.018:rm=0.018:bm=-0.018:rh=0.018:bh=-0.018
```

Join the array with commas for `-vf`; do not join these fragments with semicolons. `colorArgs()` performs the join for you.

Temperature is an approximation, not a Kelvin white balance: `+100` warms by +0.15 red and -0.15 blue; `-100` does the reverse. Use a LUT or a proper color-managed workflow when exact white balance matters.

Denoise presets:

| Value | Filter |
|---|---|
| `light` | `hqdn3d=2:1.5:3:2.25` |
| `medium` / `true` | `hqdn3d=4:3:6:4.5` |
| `strong` | `hqdn3d=6:4:9:6` |
| `nlmeans` | `nlmeans=s=3:r=15:p=7` |

`nlmeans` is much slower and can smear fine texture. Use it only when `hqdn3d` is not enough.

## Stabilization

Stabilization is a two-pass operation and is not a single `-vf` filter:

1. **Detect** motion and write `transforms.trf`.
2. **Transform** the input using that file, with auto-zoom to hide the borders.

`<skill>` below is the RoosterEdit base directory.

```js
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { buildStabilizePasses, colorArgs } from "<skill>/scripts/features/color.mjs";

const passes = buildStabilizePasses({
  input: "assets/source/handheld.mp4",
  workDir: "engine/tmp/stabilize",
});

let result = spawnSync("ffmpeg", passes.detect, { encoding: "utf8", windowsHide: true });
if (result.status !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr);

result = spawnSync("ffmpeg", passes.transform, { encoding: "utf8", windowsHide: true });
if (result.status !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr);

// Grade the stabilized intermediate in a second encode, or append the color
// filters to the transform pass to encode once.
const grade = colorArgs({
  input: passes.output,
  output: "renders/graded.mp4",
  color: plan.color,
});
```

`passes.detect` and `passes.transform` are ready-to-spawn argument arrays. `passes.transformsFile` is the detection file; `passes.output` defaults to `<workDir>/stabilized.mp4`. The caller must create `workDir` first.

Run both passes on the same input and dimensions. If the clip is trimmed or resized between passes, rerun detection. To combine stabilization and color in one encode, append `buildColorFilters(plan.color).join(",")` after `vidstabtransform=...` in the transform filter.

## FFmpeg integration

`colorArgs({ input, output, color })` returns complete arguments for a graded encode. It does not resolve paths; pass paths valid from the FFmpeg `cwd`. LUT and transforms paths are escaped for Windows drive letters.

```js
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { colorArgs } from "<skill>/scripts/features/color.mjs";

const args = colorArgs({
  input: "assets/source/interview.mp4",
  output: "renders/interview-graded.mp4",
  color: {
    lut: "assets/licensed/luts/film.cube",
    contrast: 1.08,
    saturation: 1.12,
    temperature: 12,
    denoise: "light",
  },
});

const result = spawnSync("ffmpeg", args, {
  cwd: projectDir,
  encoding: "utf8",
  windowsHide: true,
});
if (result.status !== 0) throw new Error(result.stderr);
```

With no active filters, `colorArgs` falls back to stream copy. With filters, it re-encodes the first video stream as H.264 (`yuv420p`, CRF 18, `medium`) and copies the first audio stream. Use MP4, MOV, or MKV for the output container.

## Commands

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" color <slug> [--input <path>] [--out <path>] [--update-plan] [--skip-stabilize]
```

The command writes `assets/generated/graded.mp4`; `--update-plan` points `plan.source` at the graded file before build. When `plan.color.stabilize` is true, the command runs the two vidstab passes automatically unless `--skip-stabilize` is passed.

## QA

- Skin tones stay natural; compare before/after stills at 100%.
- Highlights are not clipped and shadows are not crushed.
- Contrast and saturation match the profile, not just the reference video.
- The LUT file exists, loads, and is licensed for delivery.
- Denoise did not erase texture or create waxiness.
- Stabilization has no black borders, warped edges, or excessive crop.
- Camera motion still feels intentional; auto-zoom is not pumping.
- Consecutive shots match in color and exposure.
- Audio is still in sync after the re-encode.
- `ffprobe` confirms resolution, fps, duration, pixel format, and audio stream.

## Limitations

- This is a lightweight grade, not a color-managed pipeline. There is no HDR, log conversion, gamut mapping, or per-shot matching.
- `eq` and `colorbalance` are approximations; a LUT or a dedicated grade is better for precise looks.
- Stabilization needs two passes, a writable work directory, and an FFmpeg build with the `vidstab` filters. It cannot fix rolling shutter, motion blur, or a shot with no stable frame.
- `colorArgs` ignores `color.stabilize`; the `color` command runs `buildStabilizePasses` before the grade, or use `--skip-stabilize`.
- `colorArgs` copies the audio stream. An incompatible audio codec/container combination will fail.
- Plan validation checks that a declared LUT exists and warns when `stabilize` needs the two-pass flow; it does not validate every numeric range.
- `build` does not call `colorArgs` or `buildStabilizePasses` yet; run the `color` command with `--update-plan` before building.

# Delivery

Build the package that accompanies the final render: `metadata.json`, a thumbnail, and the caption sidecars. Delivery is a separate step after build, render, and QA; nothing is uploaded automatically.

## Input and output

Inputs are the project, the approved plan, an optional render description or probe, and optional chapters:

```js
import { buildMetadata, thumbnailArgs, createThumbnail } from "./scripts/features/delivery.mjs";

const metadata = buildMetadata({
  project,                         // project.json
  plan,                            // edit/plan.json
  render: {
    video: "renders/final.mp4",
    probe: { width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 29.97, duration: 57.2 },
    captions: {
      srt: "renders/captions.srt",
      vtt: "renders/captions.vtt",
      json: "renders/captions.json"
    },
    thumbnail: "renders/thumbnail.jpg"
  },
  chapters: plan.chapters          // optional; defaults to plan.chapters
});
```

`render` may also be a path string. Actual render probe values beat plan values, which beat `project.format`. `chapters` overrides plan/project chapters when passed, even as an empty array.

Output is a `rooster.metadata/v1` object:

```json
{
  "schema": "rooster.metadata/v1",
  "title": "Demo Video",
  "description": "A short demo.",
  "tags": ["demo", "tutorial"],
  "chapters": [
    { "start": 0, "end": 30, "title": "Intro", "timestamp": "0:00" },
    { "start": 30, "end": 57.2, "title": "Second", "timestamp": "0:30" }
  ],
  "aspectRatio": "16:9",
  "width": 1920,
  "height": 1080,
  "duration": 57.2,
  "fps": 29.97,
  "files": {
    "video": "renders/final.mp4",
    "captions": {
      "srt": "renders/captions.srt",
      "vtt": "renders/captions.vtt",
      "json": "renders/captions.json"
    },
    "thumbnail": "renders/thumbnail.jpg"
  },
  "language": "en",
  "slug": "demo-video",
  "generatedAt": "2026-11-03T00:00:00.000Z"
}
```

Titles fall back from `plan.title` to `project.title`, `project.name`, and the slug. Description uses `plan.description`, `plan.summary`, then `project.description`. Tags merge and deduplicate case-insensitively. Chapters are sorted, deduplicated, and given an `end` from the next chapter or the duration. File paths use forward slashes.

## Thumbnail

`thumbnailArgs({ video, out, time })` returns `{ args, command }` and executes nothing. `createThumbnail()` calls FFmpeg with `spawnSync`; it is opt-in, creates the output directory, overwrites the target, and returns `{ ok, status, out, bytes, error, ... }` instead of throwing on FFmpeg failure.

```js
const { args, command } = thumbnailArgs({
  video: "renders/final.mp4",
  out: "renders/thumbnail.jpg",
  time: 2.5,
  width: 1280
});

const result = createThumbnail({
  video: "renders/final.mp4",
  out: "renders/thumbnail.jpg",
  time: 2.5,
  width: 1280,
  height: 720
});
```

`out` must be `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, or `.png`. `time` accepts seconds or `HH:MM:SS(.ms)`. Width or height alone preserves aspect; both set an exact size. JPEG quality defaults to 2 (best) and accepts 2–31.

## Build integration

- Run delivery after the final render and after the caption sidecars exist.
- `metadata.json` belongs in `renders/` with `final.mp4`, `captions.srt`, `captions.vtt`, and `thumbnail.jpg`.
- The current `build` and `render` commands do not create these files or burn captions.
- Do not upload anywhere without explicit permission. Keep the render, caption, and license decisions in `qa/report.md` and `review.md`.

## Commands

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" deliver <slug> [--video <path>] [--thumb <path>] [--time 2.5]
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" captions <slug> [--out <dir>]
```

`deliver` writes `renders/thumbnail.jpg` and `renders/metadata.json`, and references caption sidecars when they exist. It does not upload anything.

## QA

- Title, description, tags, and chapters match the approved plan.
- The first chapter starts at `0:00`; chapters are sorted and within the duration.
- Aspect ratio, width, height, fps, and duration match the render probe.
- Every path in `files` exists and uses the intended case and extension.
- Captions are present and valid, or the delivery records why they are absent.
- The thumbnail is from the intended moment, readable at small size, and not a black frame.
- No unlicensed music, footage, fonts, or thumbnails are included.
- Nothing is published without explicit user permission.

## Limitations

- No platform API upload, scheduling, or OAuth.
- No automatic thumbnail composition, text overlay, or A/B variants; this extracts one frame.
- No YouTube/TikTok field validation (title length, tag limits, chapter minimums).
- Without a render probe, duration falls back to the plan or project length, which may be the source duration rather than the cut result.
- Chapter ends are inferred; the module does not rewrite the video to create chapters.
- FFmpeg must be installed for `createThumbnail`; `thumbnailArgs` works without it.
- The metadata object is not written to disk by this module; the `deliver` command owns the file write.

# Motion: real zooms and transitions

`scripts/features/motion.mjs` turns the `zoom` and `transition` element types into real motion. It is pure and dependency-free: helpers return CSS, HTML, GSAP, or interpolation values, and never write files or import `rooster.mjs`. Wire them into `renderHyperFramesHtml`, `renderHyperFramesElement`, or `renderRemotionTsx` after the module is reviewed.

## See what is planned

`plan.html` and `plan.md` include a **Motions** section: each resolved template, how many elements use it, the timecodes, a sample, and a small visual preview. The elements table also has a `Motion` column. This is the fastest way to review the motion language before the build.

To list it from the CLI:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" motions <slug>
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" motions <slug> --json
```

It shows:

- **Planned motions** grouped by resolved template (`title`, `chapter`, `diagram`, `counter`, `list`, `lower-third`, `emphasis`, `terminal`, `end-card`, `callout`, `broll`, `zoom`, `transition`, `custom`);
- **Reusable components** found under `style/components/` (project, channel, or profile scope), with their paths;
- the **built-in template catalog**, including what each one does.

`custom` means the element references a reusable component folder with `element.html`, `element.css`, and `element.js`. If the plan says `custom` but the components list is empty, the plan is pointing at a motion that does not exist yet.

## Plan shapes

### Zoom

```json
{
  "id": "el-003",
  "type": "zoom",
  "start": 52.0,
  "end": 55.0,
  "scale": 1.18,
  "originX": 0.5,
  "originY": 0.4,
  "description": "Slow punch-in on the speaker at the key insight"
}
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `start`, `end` | yes | Seconds. The zoom ramps in at `start`, holds, and returns to `1` by `end`. |
| `scale` | no | Target scale, default `1.12`. Clamped to `0.5–4`; values below `1` zoom out. |
| `originX`, `originY` | no | Transform origin as `0–1` fractions of the target. Default `0.5, 0.5`. |
| `release` | no | Default `true`. Set `false` to hold the scale at `end` instead of returning to `1`. |
| `rampIn`, `rampOut` | no | Seconds for the in/out ramp. Defaults are capped at half the element duration. |
| `ease`, `easeOut` | no | GSAP ease names. Defaults: `power2.out` and `power2.inOut`. |

### Transition

```json
{
  "id": "el-004",
  "type": "transition",
  "start": 12.1,
  "end": 12.7,
  "kind": "dip",
  "direction": "left",
  "description": "Dip to black over the chapter cut"
}
```

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `start`, `end` | yes | Seconds. The cut belongs at the midpoint (`start + (end - start) / 2`). |
| `kind` | yes | `fade`, `dip`, or `slide`. |
| `direction` | slide only | Direction of travel: `left`, `right`, `up`, or `down`. `left` enters from the right. |
| `color` | no | Overlay color. `dip` defaults to black; `fade` and `slide` default to `theme.bg`. |
| `opacity` | no | Peak opacity for `fade`/`dip`. Default `0.8` for fade and `1` for dip. |
| `easeIn`, `easeOut` | no | GSAP ease names for the two halves. Slide defaults to `power2.inOut` on both. |

`fade` is a soft fade through a color. `dip` goes fully to a solid color, usually black. `slide` is a solid panel that enters from one edge, covers the cut, and leaves through the opposite edge. It is not a push of the footage.

## API

| Export | Returns |
|---|---|
| `normalizeZoom(element, options)` | Normalized times, scale, origin, ramp, and input/output ranges. |
| `normalizeTransition(element, options)` | Normalized times, kind, direction, color, midpoint, and peak opacity. |
| `hyperframesZoom(element, selector, options)` | `{ selector, css, tween, values }`. |
| `hyperframesTransition(element, theme, options)` | `{ id, selector, html, css, tween, values }`. |
| `hyperframesZoomCss`, `hyperframesZoomTween` | The individual CSS or GSAP string. |
| `hyperframesTransitionHtml`, `hyperframesTransitionCss`, `hyperframesTransitionTween` | The individual HTML, CSS, or GSAP string. |
| `remotionZoomValues`, `remotionTransitionValues` | Frame ranges, output ranges, and `styleAt(frame)`. |
| `remotionZoomSnippet`, `remotionTransitionSnippet` | Copy-paste Remotion statements. |

## HyperFrames

```js
import {
  hyperframesZoom,
  hyperframesTransition,
} from "./features/motion.mjs";

// Zoom: target a dedicated wrapper, not the base ken-burns element.
const zoom = hyperframesZoom(zoomElement, "#zoom-layer");
// Append zoom.css to the page <style>.
// Append zoom.tween to the GSAP timeline.

// Transition: markup, CSS, and tween in one bundle.
const transition = hyperframesTransition(transitionElement, theme);
// The default id is "rooster-transition-<element id>".
// Insert transition.html with the other elements.
// Append transition.css to <style> and transition.tween to the timeline.
```

The GSAP snippets expect a paused timeline named `tl`. Pass `{ timeline: "master" }` if the integration uses another name. The helpers do not assume an element id beyond the selector argument.

Wrap the base media in a zoom layer when the existing base tween already animates `scale`. Two GSAP tweens writing `scale` to the same element will fight, and the last one wins. If a wrapper is not possible, pass `#base` and disable the base scale tween while a zoom is active.

## Remotion

```js
import {
  remotionZoomValues,
  remotionTransitionValues,
} from "./features/motion.mjs";

const z = remotionZoomValues(zoomElement, fps);
const scale = interpolate(frame, z.inputRange, z.outputRange, {
  extrapolateLeft: "clamp",
  extrapolateRight: "clamp",
});
// <div style={{ transform: `scale(${scale})`, transformOrigin: z.transformOrigin }}>

const t = remotionTransitionValues(transitionElement, fps, { theme });
const opacity = interpolate(frame, t.inputRange, t.outputRange, {
  extrapolateLeft: "clamp",
  extrapolateRight: "clamp",
});
// <div style={{ position: "absolute", inset: 0, background: t.color, opacity, pointerEvents: "none" }} />
```

`remotionZoomSnippet(element, { fps })` and `remotionTransitionSnippet(element, { fps, theme })` return copy-paste statements when editing the generated TSX by hand. `styleAt(frame)` on either values object returns the same style inline, which is easier to use inside a mapped element component.

## Cut smoothing

The cut pass is separate from the plan's `zoom`/`transition` elements. It makes silence cuts feel less dry without extra footage:

- **Audio micro-fade**: 35 ms in/out at every join. It removes clicks and softens hard consonants. `--cut-fade 0` disables it.
- **Punch-in**: an uncovered silence cut toggles a 3.5% scale (center crop) on the following clip, so consecutive shots read as wide/tight instead of a hard jump. A b-roll or transition that overlaps the join suppresses the punch. `--cut-punch 1` disables it; `--cut-punch 1.06` makes it stronger.
- **Coverage report**: `plan --check` lists long jumps with no visual cover. Add a `broll` with `layout: "pip"` or `"split"`, or a `transition`, at the join.

FilmCraft limitation: FilmCraft does not animate the base clip's scale, so `zoom` and overlay `transition` elements are not rendered by the FilmCraft target. `build` now fails with a clear message unless you pass `--allow-skipped-elements`. Use HyperFrames or Remotion when the plan needs real zooms/transitions, or replace them with `punch-in` coverage.

## Build integration

`build` now reads `zoom` and `transition` elements from `edit/plan.json`:

- HyperFrames gets the transition overlay HTML/CSS and the GSAP zoom/transition tweens; a base scale tween is disabled while a zoom is active.
- Remotion gets `motion.inputRange` / `motion.outputRange` data in `src/data/plan.ts`; the generated component applies the zoom to the base wrapper and renders the transition overlay.

Preview both engines at delivery resolution. The generated code is deterministic, but the plan still owns timing and placement.

## Timing rules

- Put the cut at the transition midpoint. A 0.6 s transition starts 0.3 s before the cut and ends 0.3 s after it.
- Keep transitions between about 0.25 s and 0.8 s. Longer is a scene device, not a cut.
- A zoom should reach its target quickly (0.4–0.6 s), hold through the insight, and release before the next visual beat.
- Do not overlap two zooms on the same selector. Do not stack a transition over another full-screen transition.
- Remotion frame ranges come from seconds and are clamped to whole frames. Very short effects below one frame collapse to one frame per step.

## QA

- Scrub the whole effect: no snap at `start`, no snap at the release, and no scale left applied afterward.
- Check the origin keeps the face or action inside frame, especially after reframing to `9:16`.
- Confirm the transition midpoint matches the cut; a frame of the old shot under a fade means the cut and the overlay are misaligned.
- Confirm the transition is fully off-screen or transparent after `end`; a lingering overlay is a full-screen color wash.
- Check at delivery resolution, not only in the preview pane.
- Watch for competing motion: base scale, zoom, and a slide overlay should not fight.

## Limitations

- Zoom is a 2D scale on one target. It is not a 3D camera, parallax, or depth effect.
- Transitions are overlays. There is no true cross-dissolve between two clips, no push of the footage, and no per-pixel wipe. Use FFmpeg `xfade` or an engine transition when the edit needs those.
- `slide` moves a solid panel, not the incoming shot.
- `release: false` leaves the target scaled. Reset it with a later tween, a cut, or a `scale: 1` statement.
- The helpers do not edit `rooster.mjs`; the render functions must import and call them.
- Selectors are trusted strings. Do not build a selector from untrusted plan text.
